We plan a return visit in 2020 - that will be our 5th trip to visit this incredible place where the guides, trackers, and all the staff make this such a memorable experience for all that visit.

Born in New York and settled down in Hong Kong for the past 20 years after living in London and Tokyo.  I "found" Londolozi in 2009 and have been a regular visitor since.  Over that time I have gained a passion for the bush and the photographic opportunities it provides.  Thanks to the tutelage of the Londolozi rangers and Creative hub I am getting my photography to an acceptable level.
Alan and I have been ambassadors for many years, this is our favorite place on earth ?

Bronwyn is 4th generation custodian of Londolozi Game Reserve, a mother, Master life coach and also one of its most longstanding employees, having grown up on the floors of the kitchen and in the gardens of the lodge.  Bronwyn’s official title is that of Londolozi’s Creative Director and as such she has spearheaded the reinvention of the Londolozi brand from 2007 until present day. In 2018, Bronwyn led the creation of the Londolozi Healing House, establishing one of the safari industry’s most innovative wellness offerings.  By weaving healing, mindfulness, and nature-based transformation into the guest experience, she helped reinvent the concept of wilderness wellness in the safari space.
Hopelessly addicted and devoted to leopards.

Love nature, watching animals and going on safari. Been lots of times on safari to different African countries. Londolozi is one of my favourite places. I am always looking forward to my next trip to Londolozi!

As a young boy growing up on an agricultural farm in Zimbabwe, Sean spent every opportunity entertaining himself outdoors, camping in the local nature reserve and learning about all facets of the natural world.  

After completing a Bachelor of Science degree in Environmental Science in Cape Town, Sean was free to follow his nature ambitions and return to his bush-loving childhood dreams, which led him to Londolozi.

Going into semi-retirement on the guiding front in 2020 saw Sean settle into a far more permanent role in the LCH, focusing his efforts on producing media content for the Londolozi online space.

Garrett has always had an incredible love for the wilderness and found his way to Londolozi straight after University. After spending time as a Londolozi Camp Manager, the incredible stories of daily sightings from his ranger counterparts and guests alike pushed him to become a Londolozi Guide, where he enjoyed 3 years in the field sharing Londolozi with thousands of guests. After a brief sabbatical travelling through Southern Africa and working in Tanzania, Garrett returned to the Londolozi Family as Sales Manager sharing Londolozi with as many people as possible.

Nick was a ranger at Londolozi from 2018 - 2022. He always had a love for nature. Growing up in Johannesburg, the annual family trip to the bush (particularly the Kruger Lowveld region of South Africa) became an escape from city life. When he and his brother weren't physically in the bush, they would pretend they were by watching wildlife documentaries and making animal tracks in the garden at home. After high school, Nick spent a year teaching sport in England and then returned to South Africa to study Engineering at Stellenbosch University. It was in the mountains of Stellenbosch where Nick further cultivated his passion for nature.
Passionate about wildlife conservation and Big Cats!   Travel, family, reading, hiking, skiing, safaris!

Robbie developed a passion for the African bush from many visits to his family’s small holding in a greater conservancy just outside Johannesburg. Living in the big city his whole life, he always found refuge in the outdoors and has grown to appreciate the slower pace of life and connectivity with nature that comes with spending time in the bush. After completing his studies in Finance and Accounting at university in Cape Town he leapt at the opportunity to follow his dream by partaking in Londolozi’s 2020 ranger training programme. His dream of sharing his passion for the African bush with others is being lived and will continue to evolve as he furthers his career as a guide at Londolozi.
Self proclaimed Leopardographer.

Megan grew up at Londolozi, where her love for nature blossomed. With a degree in Visual Studies and Social Media Marketing, her journey came full circle when she joined the dynamic Londolozi Creative Hub, where her love for nature and visuals finds its perfect home. 

Guided by an unwavering love for photography, videography, and the captivating realm of visuals, Megan hopes to impart a unique and vibrant essence to each of the creative projects she takes on.

I am a published author and wildlife and travel writer, specializing is African safaris.  I have always had a deep affinity with all living creatures, even while growing up in urban Amsterdam. Going on safari has enhanced that innate connection into a lifelong passion.

Lucie and I are retired and have turned our energies to photography and videography, of which wildlife is by far the favorite subject.  We have been to Africa every 2-3 years over the last 35 years.  We have been to several camps in each of South Africa, Botswana, Kenya, Tanzania, Namibia, Uganda and Rwanda but Londolozi and Tiger Canyon are our go-to favorite places.  We are unabashedly predator-centric and aviary-sated.  And we are so thankful that the Varty family built this community-driven concept and has taught us all the meaning of "ubuntu".

Africa enthusiast; lover of all things Africa, photography, safari, and conservation. My lifelong dream of visiting Africa came true in June 2023, second trip in 2025, and third in September 2026. Londolozi is a dream destination.

I am a published writer of three non fiction books, including My Life With Leopards, the Graham Cooke Story, which was set at Londolozi in the early 1990s. I am a seasoned safari traveller, contributing publications of safari lodges and destinations to various magazines and a keen safari photographer.

acf.lol_basic_profile_excerpt: Born to the Karula Female, he arrived in 2018,established territory in northern Londolozi, a much loved and closely followed leopard.
acf.lol_basic_profile_content:
The name Hosana, in Xitsonga/Shangaan means “Little Chief.”

Heritage & Lineage

Born in February 2016 to the Karula Female in the northern sector of the Sabi Sand Reserve. While initially thought to be sired by the Tingana Male, paternity remains unconfirmed without genetic testing. Originally from the northern sector of Sabi Sand Nature Reserve, was seen a substantial amount on Djuma

Territory Evolution
His territory establishment followed several distinct phases:

Initial Nomadic Phase (2017): First recorded on Nanga Road with a hoisted kill
Exploration Phase (2018): Concentrated movements around Manyelethi River and Ximpalapala Koppie
Challenge Phase (2019): Direct confrontations with Anderson Male, showing increasing confidence
Dominant Phase (2019-2022): Dominant over Othawa, primarily seen along Londolozi’s western boundary

Physical Characteristics

3:3 spot pattern
Distinctive scar across nose from territorial disputes
Yellow-green eyes

Behavioural Notes

Strategic approach to territory acquisition
Remarkable boldness in challenging larger males, Anderson Male.
Was found with three kills in the same jackalberry tree

Final Status
Successfully established and held territory in Othawa until his death in May 2022:

Historical Significance
Represents important aspects of male leopard dynamics:

Played a key role in Anderson Male’s territorial decline
Represented changing dynamics in the northern male hierarchy
Contributed to territorial shifts north of Sand River
He was very closely followed and loved by many of SafariLive’s viewers

His rise to dominance in Othawa exemplified the complex dynamics of male leopard territorial establishment, particularly through his bold challenges against the previously dominant Anderson Male. His untimely death in May 2022 marked the end of a significant presence in the northwestern territories.
acf.lol_territory_desc: Territorial over Othawa to the west of Marthly.

acf.lol_basic_profile_excerpt: The Torchwood male holds territory falling mostly to the west of Londolozi and is infrequently seen.
acf.lol_basic_profile_content:
The Torchwood Male is a young nomadic male that has drifted in from the north of the Sabi Sands in 2013.

Born in November or December 2010 on the Torchwood property, he is now at an age at which his father would most likely have put pressure on him to move out of his territory. His father is the Mvula male (aka Leadwood Male) who is territorial to the north of us, and who we don’t see on Londolozi.

Male leopards typically disperse at around two-and-a-half years, and this is mirrored exactly in the Torchwood male, as the last photo taken of him in the North was round about June 2013. Since then he has moved around the Sabi Sand extensively, being seen in the southern, western, and now central sectors.  Currently the Torchwood male holds territory falling mostly to the west of Londolozi and is infrequently seen.

acf.lol_basic_profile_content:
Named after the Flat Rock area on the Tinga concession where he originated

Heritage & Lineage
Born in 2013 to the Porcupine Female and Mbavala Male on Tinga concession in Kruger National Park. His arrival at Londolozi in late 2016 coincided fortuitously with the death of the Robson’s 4:4 Male, allowing him to establish prime territory despite being only three years old.

Territory Evolution
His territory has developed in distinct phases:

Initial Phase (2016): Small territory west of Londolozi camps, south of Sand River
Expansion Phase (2017-2019): Extended east along the southern bank of Sand River
Peak Domain (2019-2022): Controlled approximately 30 square kilometres, including:

South of Sand River to Maxabene
Northern sections across Marthly
Prime river frontage and drainage systems

Current Phase (2023-Present): Shifting further east and north under pressure from younger males

Physical Characteristics

3:2 spot pattern
Triangle of spots on the right side of the face
Broad, impressive facial structure
Notably large for young age during territory establishment

Presumed Offspring
Successfully sired multiple offspring through strategic territory defence:

Plaque Rock Female (deceased)
Nkuwa and Finfoot Females (first intact litter raised to independence since 2012)
Likely father of recent litters from Ingrid Dam, Piccadilly, Mashaba, and Makomsava Females

Behavioural Notes
Demonstrates exceptional strategic ability:

Established territory at an unusually young age through careful expansion
Initially maintained small territory to avoid confrontation with larger males
Systematically removed rival male genetics by eliminating cubs
Shows excellent hunting abilities despite male status
Maintains notably calm demeanor around vehicles
Successfully defended territory against nomadic males throughout the prime

Historical Significance
Represents one of Londolozi’s most successful examples of male leopard strategy:

Secured prime territory at just three years old
Successfully expanded from initial small holding to vast territory
Demonstrated perfect timing in territory acquisition and expansion
Maintained genetic diversity through successful offspring
The current eastern shift shows adaptation to changing dynamics and age
Exemplifies successful male leopard territory acquisition and management

His story particularly resonates as an example of strategic territory acquisition and management, having secured prime real estate at an unusually young age and successfully defended it through his prime years.

lol_id_markings.lol_id_markings_marking: Triangle of spots on right cheek

acf.lol_territory_desc: His territory extends roughly from the Londolozi camps westwards along the Sand River over into Singita, south to most likely the Maxabene River, and slightly north of the Sand River to Sasekile Ingwe crest.

users_spotted.user_description:
James had hardly touched a camera when he came to Londolozi, but his writing skills that complemented his Honours degree in Zoology meant that he was quickly snapped up by the Londolozi blog team. 

An environment rich in photographers helped him develop the photographic skills he needed to start capturing some great images, and 2015 saw him make the move from stills photography into film as well.

James was a member of the Londolozi family from 2010 - 2021.

Bob and I live in the San Francisco Bay Area where we enjoy boating, hiking, photography and travel. After many trips to Eastern and Southern Africa, we are pleased to call Londolozi our 'African home!'

Amanda is the Head of Marketing at Londolozi & has been in the marketing & creative industry for 16 years & the health and wellness industry for 10 years. She holds a Bachelor’s degree in Psychology and Journalism from The University of Cape Town & an Honours degree in Brand Management. She's a Life Coach, an Enneagram Practitioner & Londolozi's photographer in residence. Her passion for the creative world, wilderness & wellness has led to a unique role within the Londolozi Family. She spearheaded the creation of the Photographic Studio & brings specialty retreat offerings to life at Londolozi. Amanda ensures that marketing always has deep experience at its roots.
The Londolozi Photo Studio

I arrived at Londolozi on 1 st December 1998. I was a trainee ranger and I was green behind the ears. Londolozi became my family and my home. I left in 2005 and returned later that year to get married down in the Sand River at Londolozi. I have been very fotunate to return with my wife every year since then and I have a son who is mad about tracking and anti-poaching thanks to the many hours he has spent wit me in the bush.

Born in New York and settled down in Hong Kong for the past 20 years after living in London and Tokyo.  I "found" Londolozi in 2009 and have been a regular visitor since.  Over that time I have gained a passion for the bush and the photographic opportunities it provides.  Thanks to the tutelage of the Londolozi rangers and Creative hub I am getting my photography to an acceptable level.

Passionate Londolozi Guests! Avid wildlife photographers. Supporters and advocates for the Good Work Foundation through the All Heart Fund in the USA. Restaurateurs and wine & spirits retailers in Sarasota, Florida at Michael’s On East (www.bestfood.com)

Richie is Londolozi's Director of Technology and Sustainability and the founder of the Londolozi blog. Over the past decade he has built Londolozi's online ecosystem into a platform for advocacy of the restoration and rewilding of the natural world. Today he applies that same thinking to the land itself, helping lead the Save the Sand initiative to restore the Sand River catchment that gives Londolozi its lifeblood. His work lives at the meeting point of ancient wisdom, modern technology and nature. You'll find him in the LCH at Londolozi. Come say hi on your next visit.
Following my passion for wildlife and photography
Talley Smith's father. Resident of Bermuda. Huge fan of Londolozi and Africa generally. Keen amateur photographer.

When I was 25, I spent 15 months in South Africa, in a small town called Harrismith well known to those who drive from Johannesburg to Durban as it is a classic pit stop to refuel. It is then that I first heard about Londolozi when I bought the book "the leopards of Londolozi" and promised myself that 1 day I could fulfill my dream of visiting. It took me exactly 20 years after I had moved back to France and in April 2017, at last, I brought my wife and 9-year son Antoine to what I now consider to be the nicest place on earth: Londolozi. As I couldn't help myself, we came back this year for another 4 days of pure happiness

Fell in love with Africa (Kenya) and wildlife photography 10 years ago when I saw my first leopard in a tree.   Been lucky enough to visit Kenya a few times, Botswana a couple of times and then discovered Londolozi a couple of years ago.  There is something  about this place - the people and the animals  that keeps drawing us back!

Originally from New York USA currently living in the Sunshine state of Florida in the Tampa Bay area. My first trip to Africa was in 2009 when I visited  Botswana and Zambia. My first trip to Sabi Sands South Africa was in 2011. This is where my true addiction began. I stayed at Londolozi Varty camp and fell in love with the people and the animals.  Since then I have been back six more times and returning Sept. 2023 for my 7th . I have written several blogs and enjoy sharing photos and experiences from my trips. Leopards and male lions are my favorite to photograph. At home I have my own little family including my black lion Myra and two wild dogs Max and Jack.
Serial Londo New Year visitor with Nicki and our sons Harry and Toby. Still tracking the Anderson male leopard.
Alan and I have been ambassadors for many years, this is our favorite place on earth ?

I came here for the 1st time with my husband in Feb 2010, 2nd stop on a Vic Falls-Londolozi-Cape Town trip. I'd wanted to come here for years, as my ambition was to see a leopard in the wild. We looked at the cost, thought "ouch!" then - well it is just a one-off! On our 1st game drive  we saw Vomba, so mission achieved. Then the next morning we saw Camp Pan mating with Nottens! Within 24 hours of arriving we were completely smitten, and knew we not only had to come back, but come back the next year. So began a highly expensive addiction, and my trip 3 weeks ago was my 9th consecutive year and I celebrated my 100th game drive!

Our first visit was in 2011, we returned in 2014, then again in 2017, and again in 2018.  It is favorite place to be.  We plan on coming 2020 for my 70th birthday (3/2/50) and our 50th wedding anniversary (9/5/70)
We recently visited with our daughter's family, including 8 yr old granddaughter.  She is still talking about all the wonderful things that she saw on Safari.  We were worried that it might be a little gory for her, but she reacted with vigor to the most gruesome of events.  We plan a return visit in 2020 - that will be our 5th trip to visit this incredible place where the guides, trackers, and all the staff make this such a memorable experience for all that visit.

Being surrounded by wilderness from a young age, you experience it in all of its essence. Matt was privileged enough to grow up in the Lowveld and its surroundings, sparking a great love for nature and all it has to offer, be it the sunsets, vast landscapes or amazing wildlife. As a young boy, his favourite trips were always going to the bush with family, spending time with only the best that Africa has to offer.

Matt discovered a passion that went hand-in-hand with his love for wildlife, Photography, and this is how he found his path leading to Londolozi from 2016 to 2020.
I fell in love with S. Africa in 2014 and returned again in 2018.  My next visit will be May, 2019.  My husband and I can’t get enough.  His hobby is photography and I am a professional artist.

Lucie and I are retired and have turned our energies to photography and videography, of which wildlife is by far the favorite subject.  We have been to Africa every 2-3 years over the last 35 years.  We have been to several camps in each of South Africa, Botswana, Kenya, Tanzania, Namibia, Uganda and Rwanda but Londolozi and Tiger Canyon are our go-to favorite places.  We are unabashedly predator-centric and aviary-sated.  And we are so thankful that the Varty family built this community-driven concept and has taught us all the meaning of "ubuntu".

Jemma grew up on a farm in the Midlands Meander in Kwa-Zulu Natal and studied at the University of Cape Town. With little bush experience but with many hours of au pairing, teaching English and forming a love for travel, Jemma found herself working at Londolozi as the Cubs Den Manager in January 2018. A few months later she started working for the Londolozi Creative Hub in Digital Marketing, the person behind the scenes of Londolozi's Blog and social media - and she hasn't looked back since...
Passionate about wildlife conservation and Big Cats!   Travel, family, reading, hiking, skiing, safaris!

Coming to Africa has kick-started a life of wildlife based travel for me. My first adventure was to Kenya, Tanzania and Rwanda. That trip would become one of the things that define who I am. I was bitten hard with the Africa travel bug as they say. The rest is so called history (still in the making of course), and over the years I have come to know South Africa as a second home.
Gail “GG” Rush Gould is a world traveler, writer and a 2019 “Starling”. Londolozi was one of the most magical experiences ever!

Love nature, watching animals and going on safari. Been lots of times on safari to different African countries. Londolozi is one of my favourite places. I am always looking forward to my next trip to Londolozi!
I love big cats (animals as well), cricket, and food.

As a former travel agency owner specializing is conservation tourism, I have the opportunity to travel to unique places globally. With so many places to experience, I never go to the same place twice - Until Londolozi. The people, the land and the experiences stole a piece of my heart. Whenever I find myself in Southern Africa, I make a point to find my way back.

I'm a free lance Home Economist working mostly on Masterchef a BBC cookery show. I live in England with my husband and two black Labradors. We have three grown up sons, one grandson and  granddaughter . We have visited Londolozi four times and are making a fifth visit in early June and we cant wait!!

As a young boy growing up on an agricultural farm in Zimbabwe, Sean spent every opportunity entertaining himself outdoors, camping in the local nature reserve and learning about all facets of the natural world.  

After completing a Bachelor of Science degree in Environmental Science in Cape Town, Sean was free to follow his nature ambitions and return to his bush-loving childhood dreams, which led him to Londolozi.

Going into semi-retirement on the guiding front in 2020 saw Sean settle into a far more permanent role in the LCH, focusing his efforts on producing media content for the Londolozi online space.

Garrett has always had an incredible love for the wilderness and found his way to Londolozi straight after University. After spending time as a Londolozi Camp Manager, the incredible stories of daily sightings from his ranger counterparts and guests alike pushed him to become a Londolozi Guide, where he enjoyed 3 years in the field sharing Londolozi with thousands of guests. After a brief sabbatical travelling through Southern Africa and working in Tanzania, Garrett returned to the Londolozi Family as Sales Manager sharing Londolozi with as many people as possible.

Nick was a ranger at Londolozi from 2018 - 2022. He always had a love for nature. Growing up in Johannesburg, the annual family trip to the bush (particularly the Kruger Lowveld region of South Africa) became an escape from city life. When he and his brother weren't physically in the bush, they would pretend they were by watching wildlife documentaries and making animal tracks in the garden at home. After high school, Nick spent a year teaching sport in England and then returned to South Africa to study Engineering at Stellenbosch University. It was in the mountains of Stellenbosch where Nick further cultivated his passion for nature.

California native, travel junkie, animal lover...... have traveled to Africa over a dozen times to fulfill my passion for observing animals in their natural environment. Londolozi has become my favorite place to stay, with almost yearly visits since 2019.

Robbie developed a passion for the African bush from many visits to his family’s small holding in a greater conservancy just outside Johannesburg. Living in the big city his whole life, he always found refuge in the outdoors and has grown to appreciate the slower pace of life and connectivity with nature that comes with spending time in the bush. After completing his studies in Finance and Accounting at university in Cape Town he leapt at the opportunity to follow his dream by partaking in Londolozi’s 2020 ranger training programme. His dream of sharing his passion for the African bush with others is being lived and will continue to evolve as he furthers his career as a guide at Londolozi.

Robyn grew up in Johannesburg and every family holiday was spent exploring the Lowveld or camping around Southern Africa. Her love of nature and conservation propelled her to complete her Masters degree at the University of Edinburgh’s school of Geoscience. Although this gave her a great understanding of world-wide ecological processes, she wanted to develop a better knowledge of smaller elements in the environment closer to home - birds, trees, animals and the landscape in South Africa. This lead her back to the Lowveld and to the place where her love of nature was originally ignited when she was younger.

Growing up in the small coastal town of Mtunzini, Matt's childhood was shaped by endless hours spent exploring the forests, beaches and wetlands that sparked a lifelong passion for wildlife. After completing a BSc degree, he worked in construction and landscaping before the opportunity to join Londolozi changed the course of his career. Today, as a ranger and wildlife photographer, he has the privilege of spending every day immersed in the wilderness that first inspired him as a child.
Self proclaimed Leopardographer.

Megan grew up at Londolozi, where her love for nature blossomed. With a degree in Visual Studies and Social Media Marketing, her journey came full circle when she joined the dynamic Londolozi Creative Hub, where her love for nature and visuals finds its perfect home. 

Guided by an unwavering love for photography, videography, and the captivating realm of visuals, Megan hopes to impart a unique and vibrant essence to each of the creative projects she takes on.

I am a lifelong animal lover, especially cats!  I got to fulfill my dream of going on an African safari for my 52nd birthday (it was supposed to be for my 50th but Covid interfered!).  I fell in LOVE with Londolozi, the people, and the country.  I am counting the days until I can return!!

After a few years of working in the world of economic consulting, Kate’s love of adventure, wilderness and sense of curiosity led her to move away from the city and join the Londolozi guiding team.  It was amidst her years of studying politics, philosophy and economics that her love of exploring and understanding different wilderness areas in South Africa compounded through trips with friends and family. Kate has been fortunate to travel to many different corners of the world but she’ll argue that nothing quite beats being surrounded by nature watching an African sunrise or sunset, especially at Londolozi!

Nick grew up in Johannesburg with a deep love for the outdoors. After finishing high school, he spent a formative gap year in the Zimbabwean bushveld — an experience that cemented his passion for wildlife and conservation. Although he went on to study and build a career in corporate real estate, the pull of the wilderness never faded. Now an experienced member of the Londolozi guiding team, Nick finds the greatest joy in tracking leopards and immersing himself in the intricate world of birding. He has developed a strong passion for wildlife photography, always looking to capture authentic moments in the wild.

Keagan has always had a connection with wildlife, having been lucky enough to visit Londolozi as a child. After growing up in Johannesburg, he attended boarding school in the KwaZulu Natal Midlands where weekends were spent exploring the reserve and appreciating his surroundings. Keagan further went on to study Engineering at the University of Cape Town, during which each holiday was spent with either family or friends in the Lowveld, solidifying his dream of becoming a ranger. Having joined the Londolozi team, he is now fulfilling his childhood dream of living and working in the African bush.

Wildlife Photography Enthusiast
@wildcattraveler on IG
First visited Londolozi in June 2011.  My profile picture up close with the Nkuwa female during our 2023 visit. We returned again in 2025.  Can't wait to come back again!

I am a published author and wildlife and travel writer, specializing is African safaris.  I have always had a deep affinity with all living creatures, even while growing up in urban Amsterdam. Going on safari has enhanced that innate connection into a lifelong passion.

section_profile.lol_basic_profile_excerpt: Born 2013 Kruger, seized prime territory at young age. Strategic dominance led to successful lineage before current eastward shift.
section_profile.lol_basic_profile_excerpt_alt: A dominant male leopard over the majority of the north. He took over the 4:4 Male's territory upon his elder rival's death.

section_profile.lol_basic_profile_content:
Named after the Flat Rock area on the Tinga concession where he originated

Heritage & Lineage
Born in 2013 to the Porcupine Female and Mbavala Male on Tinga concession in Kruger National Park. His arrival at Londolozi in late 2016 coincided fortuitously with the death of the Robson’s 4:4 Male, allowing him to establish prime territory despite being only three years old.

Territory Evolution
His territory has developed in distinct phases:

Initial Phase (2016): Small territory west of Londolozi camps, south of Sand River
Expansion Phase (2017-2019): Extended east along the southern bank of Sand River
Peak Domain (2019-2022): Controlled approximately 30 square kilometres, including:

South of Sand River to Maxabene
Northern sections across Marthly
Prime river frontage and drainage systems

Current Phase (2023-Present): Shifting further east and north under pressure from younger males

Physical Characteristics

3:2 spot pattern
Triangle of spots on the right side of the face
Broad, impressive facial structure
Notably large for young age during territory establishment

Presumed Offspring
Successfully sired multiple offspring through strategic territory defence:

Plaque Rock Female (deceased)
Nkuwa and Finfoot Females (first intact litter raised to independence since 2012)
Likely father of recent litters from Ingrid Dam, Piccadilly, Mashaba, and Makomsava Females

Behavioural Notes
Demonstrates exceptional strategic ability:

Established territory at an unusually young age through careful expansion
Initially maintained small territory to avoid confrontation with larger males
Systematically removed rival male genetics by eliminating cubs
Shows excellent hunting abilities despite male status
Maintains notably calm demeanor around vehicles
Successfully defended territory against nomadic males throughout the prime

Historical Significance
Represents one of Londolozi’s most successful examples of male leopard strategy:

Secured prime territory at just three years old
Successfully expanded from initial small holding to vast territory
Demonstrated perfect timing in territory acquisition and expansion
Maintained genetic diversity through successful offspring
The current eastern shift shows adaptation to changing dynamics and age
Exemplifies successful male leopard territory acquisition and management

His story particularly resonates as an example of strategic territory acquisition and management, having secured prime real estate at an unusually young age and successfully defended it through his prime years.

lol_id_markings.lol_id_markings_marking: Triangle of spots on right cheek

section_territory.lol_territory_desc: His territory extends roughly from the Londolozi camps westwards along the Sand River over into Singita, south to most likely the Maxabene River, and slightly north of the Sand River to Sasekile Ingwe crest.

After completing a Bachelor of Science degree in Environmental Science in Cape Town, Sean was free to follow his nature ambitions and return to his bush-loving childhood dreams, which led him to Londolozi.

Going into semi-retirement on the guiding front in 2020 saw Sean settle into a far more permanent role in the LCH, focusing his efforts on producing media content for the Londolozi online space.

Garrett has always had an incredible love for the wilderness and found his way to Londolozi straight after University. After spending time as a Londolozi Camp Manager, the incredible stories of daily sightings from his ranger counterparts and guests alike pushed him to become a Londolozi Guide, where he enjoyed 3 years in the field sharing Londolozi with thousands of guests. After a brief sabbatical travelling through Southern Africa and working in Tanzania, Garrett returned to the Londolozi Family as Sales Manager sharing Londolozi with as many people as possible.

Nick was a ranger at Londolozi from 2018 - 2022. He always had a love for nature. Growing up in Johannesburg, the annual family trip to the bush (particularly the Kruger Lowveld region of South Africa) became an escape from city life. When he and his brother weren't physically in the bush, they would pretend they were by watching wildlife documentaries and making animal tracks in the garden at home. After high school, Nick spent a year teaching sport in England and then returned to South Africa to study Engineering at Stellenbosch University. It was in the mountains of Stellenbosch where Nick further cultivated his passion for nature.

California native, travel junkie, animal lover...... have traveled to Africa over a dozen times to fulfill my passion for observing animals in their natural environment. Londolozi has become my favorite place to stay, with almost yearly visits since 2019.

Robbie developed a passion for the African bush from many visits to his family’s small holding in a greater conservancy just outside Johannesburg. Living in the big city his whole life, he always found refuge in the outdoors and has grown to appreciate the slower pace of life and connectivity with nature that comes with spending time in the bush. After completing his studies in Finance and Accounting at university in Cape Town he leapt at the opportunity to follow his dream by partaking in Londolozi’s 2020 ranger training programme. His dream of sharing his passion for the African bush with others is being lived and will continue to evolve as he furthers his career as a guide at Londolozi.

Robyn grew up in Johannesburg and every family holiday was spent exploring the Lowveld or camping around Southern Africa. Her love of nature and conservation propelled her to complete her Masters degree at the University of Edinburgh’s school of Geoscience. Although this gave her a great understanding of world-wide ecological processes, she wanted to develop a better knowledge of smaller elements in the environment closer to home - birds, trees, animals and the landscape in South Africa. This lead her back to the Lowveld and to the place where her love of nature was originally ignited when she was younger.

Growing up in the small coastal town of Mtunzini, Matt's childhood was shaped by endless hours spent exploring the forests, beaches and wetlands that sparked a lifelong passion for wildlife. After completing a BSc degree, he worked in construction and landscaping before the opportunity to join Londolozi changed the course of his career. Today, as a ranger and wildlife photographer, he has the privilege of spending every day immersed in the wilderness that first inspired him as a child.
Self proclaimed Leopardographer.

Megan grew up at Londolozi, where her love for nature blossomed. With a degree in Visual Studies and Social Media Marketing, her journey came full circle when she joined the dynamic Londolozi Creative Hub, where her love for nature and visuals finds its perfect home. 

Guided by an unwavering love for photography, videography, and the captivating realm of visuals, Megan hopes to impart a unique and vibrant essence to each of the creative projects she takes on.

I am a lifelong animal lover, especially cats!  I got to fulfill my dream of going on an African safari for my 52nd birthday (it was supposed to be for my 50th but Covid interfered!).  I fell in LOVE with Londolozi, the people, and the country.  I am counting the days until I can return!!

After a few years of working in the world of economic consulting, Kate’s love of adventure, wilderness and sense of curiosity led her to move away from the city and join the Londolozi guiding team.  It was amidst her years of studying politics, philosophy and economics that her love of exploring and understanding different wilderness areas in South Africa compounded through trips with friends and family. Kate has been fortunate to travel to many different corners of the world but she’ll argue that nothing quite beats being surrounded by nature watching an African sunrise or sunset, especially at Londolozi!

Nick grew up in Johannesburg with a deep love for the outdoors. After finishing high school, he spent a formative gap year in the Zimbabwean bushveld — an experience that cemented his passion for wildlife and conservation. Although he went on to study and build a career in corporate real estate, the pull of the wilderness never faded. Now an experienced member of the Londolozi guiding team, Nick finds the greatest joy in tracking leopards and immersing himself in the intricate world of birding. He has developed a strong passion for wildlife photography, always looking to capture authentic moments in the wild.

Keagan has always had a connection with wildlife, having been lucky enough to visit Londolozi as a child. After growing up in Johannesburg, he attended boarding school in the KwaZulu Natal Midlands where weekends were spent exploring the reserve and appreciating his surroundings. Keagan further went on to study Engineering at the University of Cape Town, during which each holiday was spent with either family or friends in the Lowveld, solidifying his dream of becoming a ranger. Having joined the Londolozi team, he is now fulfilling his childhood dream of living and working in the African bush.

Wildlife Photography Enthusiast
@wildcattraveler on IG
First visited Londolozi in June 2011.  My profile picture up close with the Nkuwa female during our 2023 visit. We returned again in 2025.  Can't wait to come back again!

I am a published author and wildlife and travel writer, specializing is African safaris.  I have always had a deep affinity with all living creatures, even while growing up in urban Amsterdam. Going on safari has enhanced that innate connection into a lifelong passion.

acf.lol_basic_profile_excerpt: Saseke was a dominant female who controlled territory over most of elephant plains in the north.
acf.lol_basic_profile_content:
Saseka was a dominant female who controlled territory over most of elephant plains in the north, westward into Othawa, the western portion of Simbambili and the north western portion of Arathusa Private Game Reserve. Her major competitors were the Safari female to the east (female with one blue eye), Nyelethi female (her daughter to the south) and unknown females in the west (Othawa).

She was by far one of the most relaxed leopards in the northern sector and was photographed extensively by ODP photographic tours, who would photograph her almost exclusively. As a result she appears in the books “game drive” and “Greater Kruger- The Big Picture” by the Van den bergs.

Her main ID characteristics were a 3:3 spot pattern and she had a slight kink in her right ear.

She is estimated to have been born around 1995, but where she came from is only speculation.

She raised at least two sets of cubs successfully. The Nyelethi 4:4 female, born 14 January 2003 (sired by Mafufnyane male) was raised to independence and moved south into Marthly. The female referred to as “Salayeshe” was born in the next litter. Salayeshe had a sibling which was presumed to have been killed by a hyena. She was raised to independence and when Saseke disappeared around 2008, Salayeshe “inherited” her territory.

No one knows how Saseke died, she was last seen close to the Othawa break and was never seen again after that.
acf.lol_territory_desc: This female's territory touched a tiny portion of Londolozi in northern Marthly.

acf.lol_basic_profile_excerpt: A gorgeous golden female, this leopard spent much of her time around the Singita camps, and was even known to den cubs in the lodge.
acf.lol_basic_profile_content:
The Ravenscourt female established territory to the west of Londolozi, quickly becoming the mainstay of the leopard viewing on our neighbour, Singita’s, property.

She was famous for denning her cubs in or around the rooms at Boulders Lodge, forcing the lodge to close a particular room while she was using it to stash her cubs.

She was killed in a dramatic fight with the Nyelethi 4:3 male in 2014, in which she defended her surviving cub from his attack in the branches of a leadwood tree. Racing up the trunk, she leaped outwards, tackling the Nyelethi male out of the fork, and the two plummeted to the ground. In the ensuing scuffle, she was bitten on the back of the neck and died instantly.

Her cub survived, and established territory on Singita where he is known as the Ravenscout male.

acf.lol_basic_profile_excerpt: This leopard was born to the Nyelethi female in March 2008, but sadly did not live long enough to establish herself.
acf.lol_basic_profile_content:
This leopard was born to the Nyelethi female in March 2008, but sadly did not live long enough to establish herself among the more prominent Londolozi leopards.

Upon independence she spent much time in the east of her mother’s territory, around Nanga road and further east towards the Maliliwane drainage line, but she was killed by one of the Majingilane male lions to the north of the Londolozi boundary in September 2010.
acf.lol_territory_desc: At the time of her death this leopard was just becoming territorial around north-eastern Marthly. This territory is now held by the Nanga and Malilwane females and varies from riverine bush to mixed woodland and combretum dominated thickets. A prevalence of water in the area means there is a decent variety of game to be found here year round.

acf.lol_basic_profile_excerpt: Having been viewed by vehicles from an early age, this leopard is supremely relaxed around Land Rovers.
acf.lol_basic_profile_content:
Named after the Ximungwe Road in the western sector of her territory, ‘ximungwe’ is a bateleur in Shangaan.

Heritage & Lineage

Born in May 2015 to the Mashaba Female and sired by the Robson’s/4:4 Male, she represents the continuation of the prestigious Sunsetbend lineage. Born as part of a litter of two, though her sibling disappeared around 4-5 months of age.

Territory

Maintains a strong presence in central Londolozi, having inherited much of her territory from her mother, the Mashaba Female. Her range extends through the central parts of Sparta, an area she’s successfully defended since independence. The proximity of her territory to camp has made her one of Londolozi’s most frequently viewed leopards.

Physical Characteristics

5:3 spot pattern
Golden coat characteristic of the Sunsetbend lineage
Notably relaxed around vehicles since an early age

Reproductive History

The Ximungwe Female has proven to be an exceptionally successful mother:

Successful Offspring:

October 2018: Mahlahla Male (female sibling killed by Tortoise Pan Male at 7 months)
February 2021: Ntomi Male (only one cub ever seen)

Notable attempts:

December 2023: Two cubs born in Schwein Donga, killed by hyenas at 3/4 months old
October 2024: One cub denned off Warthog skull, is currently still alive.

Current Status

Currently raising her third litter of cubs, demonstrating once again her exceptional maternal skills. She continues to be one of Londolozi’s most viewed leopards, though known for occasional periods of extended absence, particularly when denning cubs.

Behavioural Notes

She is known for her exceptional hunting prowess, particularly during adverse weather conditions. Her comfort around vehicles, established from an early age, has allowed for unprecedented viewing opportunities of natural leopard behaviour. She displays an interesting pattern of periodically “disappearing” for weeks at a time, often coinciding with pregnancy or early denning periods.
A notably strategic mother, she carefully selects den sites and demonstrates excellent judgment in moving cubs when necessary. Her most recent den site selection in December 2023 showed her experienced approach to motherhood, choosing a well-protected boulder cluster that had previously proven successful for other females.
Historical Significance
The Ximungwe Female represents the successful continuation of the Sunsetbend lineage’s presence in central Londolozi. Her remarkable success rate in raising cubs to independence – particularly male cubs – is noteworthy, as young males typically face greater challenges surviving to adulthood. Her contribution to the leopard population extends beyond Londolozi’s boundaries, with her sons establishing territories in neighbouring areas.

lol_family_litters.lol_family_litters_desc: Denned off of Rocky Tugwaan, one male and one female cub. Female killed by the Tortoise Pan Male off of Pipeline.
Denned off of Three-streaked Donga. Only one cub ever viewed. Currently thriving.
Killed by hyenas at 3/4 months
Born in boulders off warthog skull/Nyamankunzi 25 October.

users_spotted.user_description: Mike Nicki Harry and Toby, we try to visit Londo once a year. We think of it as our second home and are privileged to have seen the most amazing sights, encountered wonderful animals and learned so much about the bush from some amazing guides and trackers with such knowledge.
Passionate about wildlife.

Bob and I live in the San Francisco Bay Area where we enjoy boating, hiking, photography and travel. After many trips to Eastern and Southern Africa, we are pleased to call Londolozi our 'African home!'

Passionate Londolozi Guests! Avid wildlife photographers. Supporters and advocates for the Good Work Foundation through the All Heart Fund in the USA. Restaurateurs and wine & spirits retailers in Sarasota, Florida at Michael’s On East (www.bestfood.com)

I arrived at Londolozi on 1 st December 1998. I was a trainee ranger and I was green behind the ears. Londolozi became my family and my home. I left in 2005 and returned later that year to get married down in the Sand River at Londolozi. I have been very fotunate to return with my wife every year since then and I have a son who is mad about tracking and anti-poaching thanks to the many hours he has spent wit me in the bush.
The Londolozi Photo Studio

For the past 35 years I've been amazed and inspired by wildlife from all corners of the world. Following a career in the City of London I now dedicate my time to wildlife photographer and commitment to wildlife conservation. When not travelling I volunteer for Conservation Organisations based in London. Social Media - www.janeaddey.co.uk & @addeyphotos.

Amanda is the Head of Marketing at Londolozi & has been in the marketing & creative industry for 16 years & the health and wellness industry for 10 years. She holds a Bachelor’s degree in Psychology and Journalism from The University of Cape Town & an Honours degree in Brand Management. She's a Life Coach, an Enneagram Practitioner & Londolozi's photographer in residence. Her passion for the creative world, wilderness & wellness has led to a unique role within the Londolozi Family. She spearheaded the creation of the Photographic Studio & brings specialty retreat offerings to life at Londolozi. Amanda ensures that marketing always has deep experience at its roots.

Born in New York and settled down in Hong Kong for the past 20 years after living in London and Tokyo.  I "found" Londolozi in 2009 and have been a regular visitor since.  Over that time I have gained a passion for the bush and the photographic opportunities it provides.  Thanks to the tutelage of the Londolozi rangers and Creative hub I am getting my photography to an acceptable level.
Following my passion for wildlife and photography

Work with innovative technology. Based in UK. Have lived in Africa and the Middle East. Passionate about travel, wildlife and photography. Keeping a log of all leopard sightings during trips to Londolozi over last few years!
Talley Smith's father. Resident of Bermuda. Huge fan of Londolozi and Africa generally. Keen amateur photographer.

When I was 25, I spent 15 months in South Africa, in a small town called Harrismith well known to those who drive from Johannesburg to Durban as it is a classic pit stop to refuel. It is then that I first heard about Londolozi when I bought the book "the leopards of Londolozi" and promised myself that 1 day I could fulfill my dream of visiting. It took me exactly 20 years after I had moved back to France and in April 2017, at last, I brought my wife and 9-year son Antoine to what I now consider to be the nicest place on earth: Londolozi. As I couldn't help myself, we came back this year for another 4 days of pure happiness
Alan and I have been ambassadors for many years, this is our favorite place on earth ?

Lucie and I are retired and have turned our energies to photography and videography, of which wildlife is by far the favorite subject.  We have been to Africa every 2-3 years over the last 35 years.  We have been to several camps in each of South Africa, Botswana, Kenya, Tanzania, Namibia, Uganda and Rwanda but Londolozi and Tiger Canyon are our go-to favorite places.  We are unabashedly predator-centric and aviary-sated.  And we are so thankful that the Varty family built this community-driven concept and has taught us all the meaning of "ubuntu".

Our first visit was in 2011, we returned in 2014, then again in 2017, and again in 2018.  It is favorite place to be.  We plan on coming 2020 for my 70th birthday (3/2/50) and our 50th wedding anniversary (9/5/70)
We recently visited with our daughter's family, including 8 yr old granddaughter.  She is still talking about all the wonderful things that she saw on Safari.  We were worried that it might be a little gory for her, but she reacted with vigor to the most gruesome of events.  We plan a return visit in 2020 - that will be our 5th trip to visit this incredible place where the guides, trackers, and all the staff make this such a memorable experience for all that visit.
My name is Rich and I love lions, birding and visiting Londolozi Game Reserve. I am also a keen photographer

Being surrounded by wilderness from a young age, you experience it in all of its essence. Matt was privileged enough to grow up in the Lowveld and its surroundings, sparking a great love for nature and all it has to offer, be it the sunsets, vast landscapes or amazing wildlife. As a young boy, his favourite trips were always going to the bush with family, spending time with only the best that Africa has to offer.

Matt discovered a passion that went hand-in-hand with his love for wildlife, Photography, and this is how he found his path leading to Londolozi from 2016 to 2020.

I came here for the 1st time with my husband in Feb 2010, 2nd stop on a Vic Falls-Londolozi-Cape Town trip. I'd wanted to come here for years, as my ambition was to see a leopard in the wild. We looked at the cost, thought "ouch!" then - well it is just a one-off! On our 1st game drive  we saw Vomba, so mission achieved. Then the next morning we saw Camp Pan mating with Nottens! Within 24 hours of arriving we were completely smitten, and knew we not only had to come back, but come back the next year. So began a highly expensive addiction, and my trip 3 weeks ago was my 9th consecutive year and I celebrated my 100th game drive!

Jemma grew up on a farm in the Midlands Meander in Kwa-Zulu Natal and studied at the University of Cape Town. With little bush experience but with many hours of au pairing, teaching English and forming a love for travel, Jemma found herself working at Londolozi as the Cubs Den Manager in January 2018. A few months later she started working for the Londolozi Creative Hub in Digital Marketing, the person behind the scenes of Londolozi's Blog and social media - and she hasn't looked back since...

Richie is Londolozi's Director of Technology and Sustainability and the founder of the Londolozi blog. Over the past decade he has built Londolozi's online ecosystem into a platform for advocacy of the restoration and rewilding of the natural world. Today he applies that same thinking to the land itself, helping lead the Save the Sand initiative to restore the Sand River catchment that gives Londolozi its lifeblood. His work lives at the meeting point of ancient wisdom, modern technology and nature. You'll find him in the LCH at Londolozi. Come say hi on your next visit.

Coming to Africa has kick-started a life of wildlife based travel for me. My first adventure was to Kenya, Tanzania and Rwanda. That trip would become one of the things that define who I am. I was bitten hard with the Africa travel bug as they say. The rest is so called history (still in the making of course), and over the years I have come to know South Africa as a second home.
I love big cats (animals as well), cricket, and food.

Love nature, watching animals and going on safari. Been lots of times on safari to different African countries. Londolozi is one of my favourite places. I am always looking forward to my next trip to Londolozi!

section_profile.lol_basic_profile_excerpt: Having been viewed by vehicles from an early age, this leopard is supremely relaxed around Land Rovers.
section_profile.lol_basic_profile_excerpt_alt: Having been viewed by vehicles from an early age, this leopard is supremely relaxed around vehicles.
section_profile.lol_basic_profile_content:
Named after the Ximungwe Road in the western sector of her territory, ‘ximungwe’ is a bateleur in Shangaan.

Heritage & Lineage

Born in May 2015 to the Mashaba Female and sired by the Robson’s/4:4 Male, she represents the continuation of the prestigious Sunsetbend lineage. Born as part of a litter of two, though her sibling disappeared around 4-5 months of age.

Territory

Maintains a strong presence in central Londolozi, having inherited much of her territory from her mother, the Mashaba Female. Her range extends through the central parts of Sparta, an area she’s successfully defended since independence. The proximity of her territory to camp has made her one of Londolozi’s most frequently viewed leopards.

Physical Characteristics

5:3 spot pattern
Golden coat characteristic of the Sunsetbend lineage
Notably relaxed around vehicles since an early age

Reproductive History

The Ximungwe Female has proven to be an exceptionally successful mother:

Successful Offspring:

October 2018: Mahlahla Male (female sibling killed by Tortoise Pan Male at 7 months)
February 2021: Ntomi Male (only one cub ever seen)

Notable attempts:

December 2023: Two cubs born in Schwein Donga, killed by hyenas at 3/4 months old
October 2024: One cub denned off Warthog skull, is currently still alive.

Current Status

Currently raising her third litter of cubs, demonstrating once again her exceptional maternal skills. She continues to be one of Londolozi’s most viewed leopards, though known for occasional periods of extended absence, particularly when denning cubs.

Behavioural Notes

She is known for her exceptional hunting prowess, particularly during adverse weather conditions. Her comfort around vehicles, established from an early age, has allowed for unprecedented viewing opportunities of natural leopard behaviour. She displays an interesting pattern of periodically “disappearing” for weeks at a time, often coinciding with pregnancy or early denning periods.
A notably strategic mother, she carefully selects den sites and demonstrates excellent judgment in moving cubs when necessary. Her most recent den site selection in December 2023 showed her experienced approach to motherhood, choosing a well-protected boulder cluster that had previously proven successful for other females.
Historical Significance
The Ximungwe Female represents the successful continuation of the Sunsetbend lineage’s presence in central Londolozi. Her remarkable success rate in raising cubs to independence – particularly male cubs – is noteworthy, as young males typically face greater challenges surviving to adulthood. Her contribution to the leopard population extends beyond Londolozi’s boundaries, with her sons establishing territories in neighbouring areas.

Denned off of Three-streaked Donga. Only one cub ever viewed. Currently thriving.
Killed by hyenas at 3/4 months
Born in boulders off warthog skull/Nyamankunzi 25 October.

acf.lol_basic_profile_excerpt: This female leopard is found in the deep southwestern grasslands, occupying territory on what used to be her mother's territory.
acf.lol_basic_profile_content:
The daughter of the Little Bush Female, this leopard is not often seen on Londolozi soil, spending much of her time around the fringes of her mother’s territory to the south. Having said that, the southern grassland areas of Londolozi are tough places to find leopards, so it is likely that she spends more time there than we think, but sightings are infrequent.

She has been viewed on a few occasions near Makhotini and Vertical Dams. Post-independence she has kept a relatively low profile but has since established territory to the south-west of Londolozi.
Birthing three litters of cubs since 2019.

She lost her first litter early on, the second litter was sadly killed by a snake during lockdown at 10 months old.

Successfully raised both daughters in her third litter. And is now raising two more cubs born in later 2023.

lol_family_litters.lol_family_litters_desc: Litter lost
Cub died from a snake bite at 10 months old.

acf.lol_territory_desc: This female holds a territory in south west Dudley and onto our neighbours south of that. The grasslands she inhabits have less bushbuck and nyala than the areas surrounding the river but leopards here focus their attention on catching reedbuck, impala and kudu instead.

acf.lol_basic_profile_excerpt: She is occasionally seen around the far north west corner of Londolozi, and is generally quite relaxed around vehicles.
acf.lol_basic_profile_content:
We know very little about this leopard. She is occasionally seen around the far north-west corner of Londolozi, and is generally quite relaxed around vehicles, which is surprising as her contact with people is necessarily limited. Her symmetrical 4:4 spot pattern is unmistakeable; a row of three spots on each cheek with a fourth directly above it.

In late 2014 she was seen to have suckle marks, indicating she was stashing cubs somewhere, and then in March 2015 she was found on our western boundary with a single cub of about 6-7 months, and both of them were playing with a pangolin. Since that sighting she has been viewed only once or twice.

As properties to the north of Londolozi also know so little about this female it is presumed she spends much of her time to the west of us on the Othawa property, which does not see a lot of vehicle traffic. It is presumed that she spent her first year or two being viewed by Land Rovers, hence her relaxed demeanour.

Her territory borders that of the much older Ximpalapala female, and it is quite possible that she is a daughter of this leopard.

acf.lol_territory_desc: This leopard holds a small territory that includes a small portion of north western Marthly. This area is dominated by combretum and silver cluster leaf woodland, where kudu, duiker and nyala are prevalent.

Passionate Londolozi Guests! Avid wildlife photographers. Supporters and advocates for the Good Work Foundation through the All Heart Fund in the USA. Restaurateurs and wine & spirits retailers in Sarasota, Florida at Michael’s On East (www.bestfood.com)

Born in New York and settled down in Hong Kong for the past 20 years after living in London and Tokyo.  I "found" Londolozi in 2009 and have been a regular visitor since.  Over that time I have gained a passion for the bush and the photographic opportunities it provides.  Thanks to the tutelage of the Londolozi rangers and Creative hub I am getting my photography to an acceptable level.

Amanda is the Head of Marketing at Londolozi & has been in the marketing & creative industry for 16 years & the health and wellness industry for 10 years. She holds a Bachelor’s degree in Psychology and Journalism from The University of Cape Town & an Honours degree in Brand Management. She's a Life Coach, an Enneagram Practitioner & Londolozi's photographer in residence. Her passion for the creative world, wilderness & wellness has led to a unique role within the Londolozi Family. She spearheaded the creation of the Photographic Studio & brings specialty retreat offerings to life at Londolozi. Amanda ensures that marketing always has deep experience at its roots.

When I was 25, I spent 15 months in South Africa, in a small town called Harrismith well known to those who drive from Johannesburg to Durban as it is a classic pit stop to refuel. It is then that I first heard about Londolozi when I bought the book "the leopards of Londolozi" and promised myself that 1 day I could fulfill my dream of visiting. It took me exactly 20 years after I had moved back to France and in April 2017, at last, I brought my wife and 9-year son Antoine to what I now consider to be the nicest place on earth: Londolozi. As I couldn't help myself, we came back this year for another 4 days of pure happiness

James had hardly touched a camera when he came to Londolozi, but his writing skills that complemented his Honours degree in Zoology meant that he was quickly snapped up by the Londolozi blog team. 

An environment rich in photographers helped him develop the photographic skills he needed to start capturing some great images, and 2015 saw him make the move from stills photography into film as well.

James was a member of the Londolozi family from 2010 - 2021.

Bob and I live in the San Francisco Bay Area where we enjoy boating, hiking, photography and travel. After many trips to Eastern and Southern Africa, we are pleased to call Londolozi our 'African home!'

California native, travel junkie, animal lover...... have traveled to Africa over a dozen times to fulfill my passion for observing animals in their natural environment. Londolozi has become my favorite place to stay, with almost yearly visits since 2019.

Being surrounded by wilderness from a young age, you experience it in all of its essence. Matt was privileged enough to grow up in the Lowveld and its surroundings, sparking a great love for nature and all it has to offer, be it the sunsets, vast landscapes or amazing wildlife. As a young boy, his favourite trips were always going to the bush with family, spending time with only the best that Africa has to offer.

Matt discovered a passion that went hand-in-hand with his love for wildlife, Photography, and this is how he found his path leading to Londolozi from 2016 to 2020.

I came here for the 1st time with my husband in Feb 2010, 2nd stop on a Vic Falls-Londolozi-Cape Town trip. I'd wanted to come here for years, as my ambition was to see a leopard in the wild. We looked at the cost, thought "ouch!" then - well it is just a one-off! On our 1st game drive  we saw Vomba, so mission achieved. Then the next morning we saw Camp Pan mating with Nottens! Within 24 hours of arriving we were completely smitten, and knew we not only had to come back, but come back the next year. So began a highly expensive addiction, and my trip 3 weeks ago was my 9th consecutive year and I celebrated my 100th game drive!

Jemma grew up on a farm in the Midlands Meander in Kwa-Zulu Natal and studied at the University of Cape Town. With little bush experience but with many hours of au pairing, teaching English and forming a love for travel, Jemma found herself working at Londolozi as the Cubs Den Manager in January 2018. A few months later she started working for the Londolozi Creative Hub in Digital Marketing, the person behind the scenes of Londolozi's Blog and social media - and she hasn't looked back since...

Richie is Londolozi's Director of Technology and Sustainability and the founder of the Londolozi blog. Over the past decade he has built Londolozi's online ecosystem into a platform for advocacy of the restoration and rewilding of the natural world. Today he applies that same thinking to the land itself, helping lead the Save the Sand initiative to restore the Sand River catchment that gives Londolozi its lifeblood. His work lives at the meeting point of ancient wisdom, modern technology and nature. You'll find him in the LCH at Londolozi. Come say hi on your next visit.
Alan and I have been ambassadors for many years, this is our favorite place on earth ?

Bronwyn is 4th generation custodian of Londolozi Game Reserve, a mother, Master life coach and also one of its most longstanding employees, having grown up on the floors of the kitchen and in the gardens of the lodge.  Bronwyn’s official title is that of Londolozi’s Creative Director and as such she has spearheaded the reinvention of the Londolozi brand from 2007 until present day. In 2018, Bronwyn led the creation of the Londolozi Healing House, establishing one of the safari industry’s most innovative wellness offerings.  By weaving healing, mindfulness, and nature-based transformation into the guest experience, she helped reinvent the concept of wilderness wellness in the safari space.

As a former travel agency owner specializing is conservation tourism, I have the opportunity to travel to unique places globally. With so many places to experience, I never go to the same place twice - Until Londolozi. The people, the land and the experiences stole a piece of my heart. Whenever I find myself in Southern Africa, I make a point to find my way back.

As a young boy growing up on an agricultural farm in Zimbabwe, Sean spent every opportunity entertaining himself outdoors, camping in the local nature reserve and learning about all facets of the natural world.  

After completing a Bachelor of Science degree in Environmental Science in Cape Town, Sean was free to follow his nature ambitions and return to his bush-loving childhood dreams, which led him to Londolozi.

Going into semi-retirement on the guiding front in 2020 saw Sean settle into a far more permanent role in the LCH, focusing his efforts on producing media content for the Londolozi online space.

Garrett has always had an incredible love for the wilderness and found his way to Londolozi straight after University. After spending time as a Londolozi Camp Manager, the incredible stories of daily sightings from his ranger counterparts and guests alike pushed him to become a Londolozi Guide, where he enjoyed 3 years in the field sharing Londolozi with thousands of guests. After a brief sabbatical travelling through Southern Africa and working in Tanzania, Garrett returned to the Londolozi Family as Sales Manager sharing Londolozi with as many people as possible.

Nick was a ranger at Londolozi from 2018 - 2022. He always had a love for nature. Growing up in Johannesburg, the annual family trip to the bush (particularly the Kruger Lowveld region of South Africa) became an escape from city life. When he and his brother weren't physically in the bush, they would pretend they were by watching wildlife documentaries and making animal tracks in the garden at home. After high school, Nick spent a year teaching sport in England and then returned to South Africa to study Engineering at Stellenbosch University. It was in the mountains of Stellenbosch where Nick further cultivated his passion for nature.

Megan grew up at Londolozi, where her love for nature blossomed. With a degree in Visual Studies and Social Media Marketing, her journey came full circle when she joined the dynamic Londolozi Creative Hub, where her love for nature and visuals finds its perfect home. 

Guided by an unwavering love for photography, videography, and the captivating realm of visuals, Megan hopes to impart a unique and vibrant essence to each of the creative projects she takes on.
First visited Londolozi in June 2011.  My profile picture up close with the Nkuwa female during our 2023 visit. We returned again in 2025.  Can't wait to come back again!

section_profile.lol_basic_profile_excerpt_alt: She is occasionally seen around the far north west corner of and is quite relaxed around vehicles.
section_profile.lol_basic_profile_content:
We know very little about this leopard. She is occasionally seen around the far north-west corner of Londolozi, and is generally quite relaxed around vehicles, which is surprising as her contact with people is necessarily limited. Her symmetrical 4:4 spot pattern is unmistakeable; a row of three spots on each cheek with a fourth directly above it.

In late 2014 she was seen to have suckle marks, indicating she was stashing cubs somewhere, and then in March 2015 she was found on our western boundary with a single cub of about 6-7 months, and both of them were playing with a pangolin. Since that sighting she has been viewed only once or twice.

As properties to the north of Londolozi also know so little about this female it is presumed she spends much of her time to the west of us on the Othawa property, which does not see a lot of vehicle traffic. It is presumed that she spent her first year or two being viewed by Land Rovers, hence her relaxed demeanour.

Her territory borders that of the much older Ximpalapala female, and it is quite possible that she is a daughter of this leopard.

acf.lol_basic_profile_excerpt: One of the bigger male leopards seen on Londolozi in recent years, the Emsagwen male wasn’t often encountered.
acf.lol_basic_profile_content:
One of the bigger male leopards seen on Londolozi in recent years, the Emsagwen male wasn’t often encountered, since most of his territory fell outside our borders. He was occasionally seen in the NE reaches of Londolozi, but sightings were infrequent at best.

He was initially unrelaxed around vehicles, and it is therefore assumed that he originated in the Kruger National Park. His initial territory lay along the eastern border of the Sabi Sands and Kruger.

His disappearance in the latter parts of 2011 remains a mystery, but there were some suggestions that he had met his fate at the hands of a pride of lions.  His death left a territory vacant, and the Dudley Riverbank 5:5 male, who was battling for territory with the Camp Pan male at the time, moved across to fill the gap, granting the Camp Pan male a lifeline.

acf.lol_basic_profile_excerpt: He was born in 2009 in a litter of three, with his siblings being the Nanga female and Nyelethi 4:3 male.
acf.lol_basic_profile_content:
Little is known of the fate of this male.  He was born in 2009 in a litter of three, with his siblings being the Nanga female and Nyelethi 4:3 male, who established territory in the western sector of the Sabi Sands. It is very unusual for a litter of three to all survive to independence.

The last records of him are on Londolozi soil, and he was last seen in the early parts of 2012. As a young independent male, he would have had to survive at least a few years before being old and big enough to establish a territory of his own. Whether he managed to do this or not remains a mystery. No records of him after 2012 exist, but it is certainly possible that he displaced to the Kruger National Park. Since leopards – males in particular – regularly displace into the Sabi Sands from KNP, they can easily displace the other way.

He may have been killed by a rival predator, but we hope he made it into the Kruger and established a reign as successful as his brother.

acf.lol_basic_profile_excerpt: Unofficially the biggest leopard in the Sabi Sands, the Anderson male is an absolutely enormous individual in north western Londolozi.
acf.lol_basic_profile_content:
One of the biggest leopards in the Sabi Sands, the Anderson male is an absolutely enormous individual who is seen in the north western sections of Londolozi, from Ximpalapala koppie up to the northern break. After the death of the Marthly male, he has been seen to push further south and eastwards, and although being seen more regularly, is not 100% relaxed around vehicles yet.

Although viewed occasionally in 2014, it was only upon the disappearance of the Marthly male that sightings of the Anderson male started becoming more frequent.

He was seen mating with the Nanga female in April and May 2016, the female having lost a young litter of cubs shortly before that.

Born in 2008, the Andreson male should still hopefully have many years left in him, and it is likely that his size will keep him firmly established in his area for some time to come.
acf.lol_territory_desc: This leopard's territory falls into north western Marthly and has progressively been stretching further south and east into Londolozi. He is predominantly seen around the Ximpalapala Koppies, an ideal vantage point or even hunting spot for the rarely seen Klipspringer. Being such a large male, it is likely he is attempting to extend his territory further south to include the hotly contested Sand River, although he has not been recorded this far south yet.

section_profile.lol_basic_profile_excerpt: Unofficially the biggest leopard in the Sabi Sands, the Anderson male is an absolutely enormous individual in north western Londolozi.
section_profile.lol_basic_profile_excerpt_alt: Unofficially one of the biggest leopard in the Sabi Sands, the Anderson male is an absolutely enormous individual in the north west.
section_profile.lol_basic_profile_content:
One of the biggest leopards in the Sabi Sands, the Anderson male is an absolutely enormous individual who is seen in the north western sections of Londolozi, from Ximpalapala koppie up to the northern break. After the death of the Marthly male, he has been seen to push further south and eastwards, and although being seen more regularly, is not 100% relaxed around vehicles yet.

Although viewed occasionally in 2014, it was only upon the disappearance of the Marthly male that sightings of the Anderson male started becoming more frequent.

He was seen mating with the Nanga female in April and May 2016, the female having lost a young litter of cubs shortly before that.

Born in 2008, the Andreson male should still hopefully have many years left in him, and it is likely that his size will keep him firmly established in his area for some time to come.

section_territory.lol_territory_desc: This leopard's territory falls into north western Marthly and has progressively been stretching further south and east into Londolozi. He is predominantly seen around the Ximpalapala Koppies, an ideal vantage point or even hunting spot for the rarely seen Klipspringer. Being such a large male, it is likely he is attempting to extend his territory further south to include the hotly contested Sand River, although he has not been recorded this far south yet.

acf.lol_basic_profile_excerpt: Another leopard who originated in the Kruger National Park, he has established a large territory in the south eastern areas of Londolozi.
acf.lol_basic_profile_content:
Another leopard who originated in the Kruger National Park, this male was unrelaxed and even aggressive towards vehicles when first viewed on the Londolozi property, and charged a number of rangers during the early months of his tenure. After repeated viewings, he relaxed far more and sightings of him became far more consistent.

He then established a large territory in the southeastern areas of Londolozi, from the Dudley Camp region along the Sand River to the eastern edge of the central grasslands. The area is relatively thick and tracking him proved to be difficult.

He was believed to have fathered the Ndzanzeni Female’s male offspring, the Tortoise Pan Male.

A serious territorial spat with the Piva male in winter of 2015 left both leopards cut up around the face and neck.

As he has aged he has lost muscle mass, but is still being seen in the eastern parts of Dudley, along the Sand River. He has still been scent marking and calling as of February 2022 but no longer roams the enormous territory he used to.
acf.lol_territory_desc: This leopard's territory falls mainly in eastern Dudley, with some of his favourite patrol routes and hunting spots falling around the Tugwaan Drainage. These areas provide ideal resting spots in the heavily shaded riverine bush, a high prey density as well as clean drinking water.
