acf.lol_basic_profile_excerpt: Born to the Tugwaan female in August 1992, this leopard would redefine the relationship between man and wild cat.
acf.lol_basic_profile_content:
Named after 3:4 spot pattern but, known affectionately as “Manana” (Mother in Shangaan) by John Varty

Heritage & Lineage
Born in August 1992 to the notoriously aggressive Tugwaan Female and granddaughter of the original Mother Leopard. Her remarkable contrast to her mother’s temperament demonstrated the individual nature of leopard personalities while maintaining the prestigious bloodline’s significance at Londolozi.

Territory
Established territory in and around the Tugwaan Drainage and surrounds, particularly favouring Nyamakunze Crest. After her death, this prime territory was inherited by her daughter, the Nottens Female, maintaining the family’s presence in this significant area.

Physical Characteristics

3:4 spot pattern
Notably relaxed demeanor around vehicles
Athletic build characteristic of the Mother Leopard lineage

Reproductive History
Demonstrated remarkable reproductive success:

Attempted to raise 8 litters by age 11
Notable successful offspring include:

Nottens Female (first litter) – lived to 18 years, Londolozi’s longest-lived recorded leopard
Dudley Riverbank Female (September 1998 litter)

Uniquely adopted and raised her grandson (Dudley Riverbank 5:5 Male) after her daughter abandoned him during a hyena attack

Current Status
Passed away in the winter of 2009 at almost 17 years of age. Her death drew visitors from far and wide to pay respects, marking the end of an era but not the end of her legacy, which continues through her descendants.

Behavioural Notes
Revolutionized understanding of leopard behaviour in several ways:

Showed extraordinary comfort around vehicles despite her mother’s aggressive nature
Demonstrated unprecedented maternal behaviour by adopting her grandson
Formed a unique bond with her adopted grandson who later provided for her in her old age
Developed a special trust relationship with John Varty
Known for remarkable hunting abilities, including documented python kills

Historical Significance
The 3:4 Female represents a pivotal figure in Londolozi’s leopard history:

Bridged the gap between her aggressive mother and the relaxed nature of future generations
Challenged conventional understanding of leopard behaviour through her adoption of her grandson
Established a significant portion of the current Mother Leopard lineage through her successful daughters
Her death in 2009 marked the end of an era, but her legacy continues through her descendants
Demonstrated the individual nature of leopard personalities, showing how offspring can differ dramatically from their parents

Her story remains one of the most compelling in Londolozi’s leopard history, particularly her unprecedented relationship with her grandson, which challenged the scientific understanding of leopard behaviour.

acf.lol_basic_profile_excerpt: Londolozi's most viewed leopard and prolific mother. This gorgeous female has raised multiple cubs to independence.
acf.lol_basic_profile_content:
Heritage & Lineage

Born in August 2012 to the Mashaba Female and sired by the Marthly Male, she carries the prestigious Sunsetbend lineage. Born as part of a litter of two, though her sibling was only briefly seen in the early days before disappearing.

Territory

Currently maintains territory in northeastern Sparta, ranging from the Sand River south to Tamboti Donga. Following the successful raising of the Plaque Rock Female, she ceded her western territory to her daughter and shifted further east. Her current territory extends no further west than Warrens Road, with a significant presence in the marula crests near the eastern boundary.

Reproductive History

The Nkoveni Female has demonstrated both remarkable success and resilience through tragedy:

Successful Offspring:

March 2018: Plaque Rock Female
February 2021: Xinkhova Female and Stone Drift Female (both reached independence)
January 2024: Currently raising one surviving cub of a litter of three.

Notable Attempts:

Mid 2016: Two cubs (litter lost)
January 2017: Two cubs denned at Trogon Dam (lost to Flat Rock Male)
March 2018: One cub denned in Sand River- Plaque Rock Female
February 2021: Two cubs denned in Mala Mala- Xinkhova and Stone Drift Females
February 2023: Two cubs (killed by Three Rivers Female)
January 2024: Three cubs denned in Mala Mala, one broke its jaw then killed by Kambula Pride at 4 months old, another killed at 10 months old by Kambula Pride.

Current Status

She is raising one young male cub from her January 2024 litter. She demonstrates incredible resilience after losing one cub to a jaw injury and recent dramatic encounters with the Kambula Pride. Despite facing significant challenges, she shows exceptional maternal care and hunting prowess.

Behavioural Notes

Her journey from a cautious cub to a confident adult is noteworthy. Initially isolated in her early months, she underwent a remarkable transformation at seven months of age, suddenly becoming notably relaxed around vehicles. She’s known for her comfort in marula trees and exceptional mothering skills, even showing remarkable attention to an injured cub before its eventual loss.

Perhaps most notably, she recently demonstrated extraordinary courage and fighting spirit in protecting her cubs from a pride of lions, managing to escape a direct confrontation through quick thinking and agility. Though she lost one cub in this encounter, her survival instincts and maternal protection helped save her remaining cub.

Historical Significance

The Nkoveni Female represents the successful continuation of the Sunsetbend lineage through multiple generations. Her success in raising multiple female offspring to independence (Plaque Rock, Xinkhova, and Stone Drift females) has significantly contributed to the leopard population dynamics at Londolozi. Her story encompasses both the triumphs and tragedies that characterize the life of a female leopard in this environment, making her one of the most well-documented and followed leopards in recent Londolozi history.

users_spotted.user_description:
James had hardly touched a camera when he came to Londolozi, but his writing skills that complemented his Honours degree in Zoology meant that he was quickly snapped up by the Londolozi blog team. 

An environment rich in photographers helped him develop the photographic skills he needed to start capturing some great images, and 2015 saw him make the move from stills photography into film as well.

James was a member of the Londolozi family from 2010 - 2021.

Bob and I live in the San Francisco Bay Area where we enjoy boating, hiking, photography and travel. After many trips to Eastern and Southern Africa, we are pleased to call Londolozi our 'African home!'

Amanda is the Head of Marketing at Londolozi & has been in the marketing & creative industry for 16 years & the health and wellness industry for 10 years. She holds a Bachelor’s degree in Psychology and Journalism from The University of Cape Town & an Honours degree in Brand Management. She's a Life Coach, an Enneagram Practitioner & Londolozi's photographer in residence. Her passion for the creative world, wilderness & wellness has led to a unique role within the Londolozi Family. She spearheaded the creation of the Photographic Studio & brings specialty retreat offerings to life at Londolozi. Amanda ensures that marketing always has deep experience at its roots.
The Londolozi Photo Studio

Mike Nicki Harry and Toby, we try to visit Londo once a year. We think of it as our second home and are privileged to have seen the most amazing sights, encountered wonderful animals and learned so much about the bush from some amazing guides and trackers with such knowledge.

Passionate Londolozi Guests! Avid wildlife photographers. Supporters and advocates for the Good Work Foundation through the All Heart Fund in the USA. Restaurateurs and wine & spirits retailers in Sarasota, Florida at Michael’s On East (www.bestfood.com)

For the past 35 years I've been amazed and inspired by wildlife from all corners of the world. Following a career in the City of London I now dedicate my time to wildlife photographer and commitment to wildlife conservation. When not travelling I volunteer for Conservation Organisations based in London. Social Media - www.janeaddey.co.uk & @addeyphotos.

Keen hobbies:  wild life and nature photography, target shooting, learning to fly fish;
Favorite places: Londolozi, Grand Teton & Yellowstone National Parks
Passionate about wildlife.
Visited Londolozi twice on a Track Your Life retreat with Boyd Varty. Love Africa, like wildlife and enjoy photography

I arrived at Londolozi on 1 st December 1998. I was a trainee ranger and I was green behind the ears. Londolozi became my family and my home. I left in 2005 and returned later that year to get married down in the Sand River at Londolozi. I have been very fotunate to return with my wife every year since then and I have a son who is mad about tracking and anti-poaching thanks to the many hours he has spent wit me in the bush.

Born in New York and settled down in Hong Kong for the past 20 years after living in London and Tokyo.  I "found" Londolozi in 2009 and have been a regular visitor since.  Over that time I have gained a passion for the bush and the photographic opportunities it provides.  Thanks to the tutelage of the Londolozi rangers and Creative hub I am getting my photography to an acceptable level.
Hopelessly addicted and devoted to leopards.
Following my passion for wildlife and photography

Work with innovative technology. Based in UK. Have lived in Africa and the Middle East. Passionate about travel, wildlife and photography. Keeping a log of all leopard sightings during trips to Londolozi over last few years!
Talley Smith's father. Resident of Bermuda. Huge fan of Londolozi and Africa generally. Keen amateur photographer.

Fell in love with Africa (Kenya) and wildlife photography 10 years ago when I saw my first leopard in a tree.   Been lucky enough to visit Kenya a few times, Botswana a couple of times and then discovered Londolozi a couple of years ago.  There is something  about this place - the people and the animals  that keeps drawing us back!

Originally from New York USA currently living in the Sunshine state of Florida in the Tampa Bay area. My first trip to Africa was in 2009 when I visited  Botswana and Zambia. My first trip to Sabi Sands South Africa was in 2011. This is where my true addiction began. I stayed at Londolozi Varty camp and fell in love with the people and the animals.  Since then I have been back six more times and returning Sept. 2023 for my 7th . I have written several blogs and enjoy sharing photos and experiences from my trips. Leopards and male lions are my favorite to photograph. At home I have my own little family including my black lion Myra and two wild dogs Max and Jack.

Richie is Londolozi's Director of Technology and Sustainability and the founder of the Londolozi blog. Over the past decade he has built Londolozi's online ecosystem into a platform for advocacy of the restoration and rewilding of the natural world. Today he applies that same thinking to the land itself, helping lead the Save the Sand initiative to restore the Sand River catchment that gives Londolozi its lifeblood. His work lives at the meeting point of ancient wisdom, modern technology and nature. You'll find him in the LCH at Londolozi. Come say hi on your next visit.
Serial Londo New Year visitor with Nicki and our sons Harry and Toby. Still tracking the Anderson male leopard.
Alan and I have been ambassadors for many years, this is our favorite place on earth ?
Here at Londolozi in awe.

Our first visit was in 2011, we returned in 2014, then again in 2017, and again in 2018.  It is favorite place to be.  We plan on coming 2020 for my 70th birthday (3/2/50) and our 50th wedding anniversary (9/5/70)
We recently visited with our daughter's family, including 8 yr old granddaughter.  She is still talking about all the wonderful things that she saw on Safari.  We were worried that it might be a little gory for her, but she reacted with vigor to the most gruesome of events.  We plan a return visit in 2020 - that will be our 5th trip to visit this incredible place where the guides, trackers, and all the staff make this such a memorable experience for all that visit.

I came here for the 1st time with my husband in Feb 2010, 2nd stop on a Vic Falls-Londolozi-Cape Town trip. I'd wanted to come here for years, as my ambition was to see a leopard in the wild. We looked at the cost, thought "ouch!" then - well it is just a one-off! On our 1st game drive  we saw Vomba, so mission achieved. Then the next morning we saw Camp Pan mating with Nottens! Within 24 hours of arriving we were completely smitten, and knew we not only had to come back, but come back the next year. So began a highly expensive addiction, and my trip 3 weeks ago was my 9th consecutive year and I celebrated my 100th game drive!

California native, travel junkie, animal lover...... have traveled to Africa over a dozen times to fulfill my passion for observing animals in their natural environment. Londolozi has become my favorite place to stay, with almost yearly visits since 2019.

Lucie and I are retired and have turned our energies to photography and videography, of which wildlife is by far the favorite subject.  We have been to Africa every 2-3 years over the last 35 years.  We have been to several camps in each of South Africa, Botswana, Kenya, Tanzania, Namibia, Uganda and Rwanda but Londolozi and Tiger Canyon are our go-to favorite places.  We are unabashedly predator-centric and aviary-sated.  And we are so thankful that the Varty family built this community-driven concept and has taught us all the meaning of "ubuntu".

Being surrounded by wilderness from a young age, you experience it in all of its essence. Matt was privileged enough to grow up in the Lowveld and its surroundings, sparking a great love for nature and all it has to offer, be it the sunsets, vast landscapes or amazing wildlife. As a young boy, his favourite trips were always going to the bush with family, spending time with only the best that Africa has to offer.

Matt discovered a passion that went hand-in-hand with his love for wildlife, Photography, and this is how he found his path leading to Londolozi from 2016 to 2020.

Jemma grew up on a farm in the Midlands Meander in Kwa-Zulu Natal and studied at the University of Cape Town. With little bush experience but with many hours of au pairing, teaching English and forming a love for travel, Jemma found herself working at Londolozi as the Cubs Den Manager in January 2018. A few months later she started working for the Londolozi Creative Hub in Digital Marketing, the person behind the scenes of Londolozi's Blog and social media - and she hasn't looked back since...

Bronwyn is 4th generation custodian of Londolozi Game Reserve, a mother, Master life coach and also one of its most longstanding employees, having grown up on the floors of the kitchen and in the gardens of the lodge.  Bronwyn’s official title is that of Londolozi’s Creative Director and as such she has spearheaded the reinvention of the Londolozi brand from 2007 until present day. In 2018, Bronwyn led the creation of the Londolozi Healing House, establishing one of the safari industry’s most innovative wellness offerings.  By weaving healing, mindfulness, and nature-based transformation into the guest experience, she helped reinvent the concept of wilderness wellness in the safari space.

Love nature, watching animals and going on safari. Been lots of times on safari to different African countries. Londolozi is one of my favourite places. I am always looking forward to my next trip to Londolozi!

As a young boy growing up on an agricultural farm in Zimbabwe, Sean spent every opportunity entertaining himself outdoors, camping in the local nature reserve and learning about all facets of the natural world.  

After completing a Bachelor of Science degree in Environmental Science in Cape Town, Sean was free to follow his nature ambitions and return to his bush-loving childhood dreams, which led him to Londolozi.

Going into semi-retirement on the guiding front in 2020 saw Sean settle into a far more permanent role in the LCH, focusing his efforts on producing media content for the Londolozi online space.

Garrett has always had an incredible love for the wilderness and found his way to Londolozi straight after University. After spending time as a Londolozi Camp Manager, the incredible stories of daily sightings from his ranger counterparts and guests alike pushed him to become a Londolozi Guide, where he enjoyed 3 years in the field sharing Londolozi with thousands of guests. After a brief sabbatical travelling through Southern Africa and working in Tanzania, Garrett returned to the Londolozi Family as Sales Manager sharing Londolozi with as many people as possible.

Nick was a ranger at Londolozi from 2018 - 2022. He always had a love for nature. Growing up in Johannesburg, the annual family trip to the bush (particularly the Kruger Lowveld region of South Africa) became an escape from city life. When he and his brother weren't physically in the bush, they would pretend they were by watching wildlife documentaries and making animal tracks in the garden at home. After high school, Nick spent a year teaching sport in England and then returned to South Africa to study Engineering at Stellenbosch University. It was in the mountains of Stellenbosch where Nick further cultivated his passion for nature.

Robbie developed a passion for the African bush from many visits to his family’s small holding in a greater conservancy just outside Johannesburg. Living in the big city his whole life, he always found refuge in the outdoors and has grown to appreciate the slower pace of life and connectivity with nature that comes with spending time in the bush. After completing his studies in Finance and Accounting at university in Cape Town he leapt at the opportunity to follow his dream by partaking in Londolozi’s 2020 ranger training programme. His dream of sharing his passion for the African bush with others is being lived and will continue to evolve as he furthers his career as a guide at Londolozi.

I am passionate about travel, photography, Africa(its people and wildlife), my family, especially my grandchildren! Going to Africa for the first time in 2010 changed my life and made me want to do wildlife expeditions! Since then I have traveled to all the continents mostly focusing on photographing wildlife! Londolozi has become one of my favorite places of all and I look forward to returning as many more times as possible! It has stolen my heart and I am humbled by the beauty of all the amazing creatures I have seen there.

Robyn grew up in Johannesburg and every family holiday was spent exploring the Lowveld or camping around Southern Africa. Her love of nature and conservation propelled her to complete her Masters degree at the University of Edinburgh’s school of Geoscience. Although this gave her a great understanding of world-wide ecological processes, she wanted to develop a better knowledge of smaller elements in the environment closer to home - birds, trees, animals and the landscape in South Africa. This lead her back to the Lowveld and to the place where her love of nature was originally ignited when she was younger.

Growing up in the small coastal town of Mtunzini, Matt's childhood was shaped by endless hours spent exploring the forests, beaches and wetlands that sparked a lifelong passion for wildlife. After completing a BSc degree, he worked in construction and landscaping before the opportunity to join Londolozi changed the course of his career. Today, as a ranger and wildlife photographer, he has the privilege of spending every day immersed in the wilderness that first inspired him as a child.

I'm a free lance Home Economist working mostly on Masterchef a BBC cookery show. I live in England with my husband and two black Labradors. We have three grown up sons, one grandson and  granddaughter . We have visited Londolozi four times and are making a fifth visit in early June and we cant wait!!

Tristan is a Zimbabwean born journalist. He grew up moving farms in his home country and moved to South Africa to attend Rhodes University. With a passion for wildlife, it was a natural progression that he gravitated to Londolozi. He worked in the creative team bringing content to our online audience.
I love Londolozi and just visited Tree Camp, my favorite camp. I look forward to coming back soon!
Self proclaimed Leopardographer.

Megan grew up at Londolozi, where her love for nature blossomed. With a degree in Visual Studies and Social Media Marketing, her journey came full circle when she joined the dynamic Londolozi Creative Hub, where her love for nature and visuals finds its perfect home. 

Guided by an unwavering love for photography, videography, and the captivating realm of visuals, Megan hopes to impart a unique and vibrant essence to each of the creative projects she takes on.

Nick grew up in Johannesburg with a deep love for the outdoors. After finishing high school, he spent a formative gap year in the Zimbabwean bushveld — an experience that cemented his passion for wildlife and conservation. Although he went on to study and build a career in corporate real estate, the pull of the wilderness never faded. Now an experienced member of the Londolozi guiding team, Nick finds the greatest joy in tracking leopards and immersing himself in the intricate world of birding. He has developed a strong passion for wildlife photography, always looking to capture authentic moments in the wild.

After a few years of working in the world of economic consulting, Kate’s love of adventure, wilderness and sense of curiosity led her to move away from the city and join the Londolozi guiding team.  It was amidst her years of studying politics, philosophy and economics that her love of exploring and understanding different wilderness areas in South Africa compounded through trips with friends and family. Kate has been fortunate to travel to many different corners of the world but she’ll argue that nothing quite beats being surrounded by nature watching an African sunrise or sunset, especially at Londolozi!

Keagan has always had a connection with wildlife, having been lucky enough to visit Londolozi as a child. After growing up in Johannesburg, he attended boarding school in the KwaZulu Natal Midlands where weekends were spent exploring the reserve and appreciating his surroundings. Keagan further went on to study Engineering at the University of Cape Town, during which each holiday was spent with either family or friends in the Lowveld, solidifying his dream of becoming a ranger. Having joined the Londolozi team, he is now fulfilling his childhood dream of living and working in the African bush.

Coming to Africa has kick-started a life of wildlife based travel for me. My first adventure was to Kenya, Tanzania and Rwanda. That trip would become one of the things that define who I am. I was bitten hard with the Africa travel bug as they say. The rest is so called history (still in the making of course), and over the years I have come to know South Africa as a second home.

I live in the wonderful State of Michigan, and I am an avid animal lover. I love to travel and see the many beautiful wonders that mother earth presents to us. Sometimes these travels allow me to see exotic animals in the wild. These by far are my most rewarding trips that leaves me with a sense of fulfillment. There is nothing more beautiful than watching the young ones being cared for by their mothers. I am married with two kids and four grandchildren and plan on bringing the family to some of my future adventures so that they too can enjoy the natural beauty of this world.

Wildlife Photography Enthusiast
@wildcattraveler on IG

I live in Canada. My first visit was June 2023 and I stayed at Tree Camp for 1 week. 
I returned in June 2024 for another week. June 2025 I have reserved 10 days at Tree Camp. Londolozi has changed me. I am on a non-stop thrill during visits. The animals, the food, the service, nothing is too much to ask for during your stay. The Healing House services are spectacular! Londolozi is a truly magical place. It makes one feel alive! That is me with the amazing John Varty in my profile photo.

Looking forward to visiting Londolozi for the first time in Sept. 2023!  Update: it was spectacular. Kyle was an amazing ranger/guide with Prof as his formidable tracker! So many sightings every day!  We look forward to our next visit.
Retired from consumer product marketing. Hobbies are sculpture, care of community perennial garden in 7 acre private park, member of several community boards.

I am a published author and wildlife and travel writer, specializing is African safaris.  I have always had a deep affinity with all living creatures, even while growing up in urban Amsterdam. Going on safari has enhanced that innate connection into a lifelong passion.
Passionate about wildlife conservation and Big Cats!   Travel, family, reading, hiking, skiing, safaris!
South African living in Canada for the past +25 years, lover of the African bush!

I live in the US but I am from Argentina. Africa has conquered my heart! Kenya, Botswana, Zimbabwe, and now South Africa. Following the concept of wildness from Craig Foster... So much to learn from traditional cultures throughout the world!
I was a physicist in my professional life. I treasure the everlasting connections with many of my former students...
First visited Londolozi in June 2011.  My profile picture up close with the Nkuwa female during our 2023 visit. We returned again in 2025.  Can't wait to come back again!

I am a published writer of three non fiction books, including My Life With Leopards, the Graham Cooke Story, which was set at Londolozi in the early 1990s. I am a seasoned safari traveller, contributing publications of safari lodges and destinations to various magazines and a keen safari photographer.
If I’m not running, I’m hanging with Jo Ann loving retired life and planning our next trip!

Though she lost one cub in this encounter, her survival instincts and maternal protection helped save her remaining cub.

Historical Significance

The Nkoveni Female represents the successful continuation of the Sunsetbend lineage through multiple generations. Her success in raising multiple female offspring to independence (Plaque Rock, Xinkhova, and Stone Drift females) has significantly contributed to the leopard population dynamics at Londolozi. Her story encompasses both the triumphs and tragedies that characterize the life of a female leopard in this environment, making her one of the most well-documented and followed leopards in recent Londolozi history.

Born in New York and settled down in Hong Kong for the past 20 years after living in London and Tokyo.  I "found" Londolozi in 2009 and have been a regular visitor since. Talley Smith's father. Resident of Bermuda. Huge fan of Londolozi and Africa generally. Keen amateur photographer.

Fell in love with Africa (Kenya) and wildlife photography 10 years ago when I saw my first leopard in a tree. Alan and I have been ambassadors for many years, this is our favorite place on earth ?
Here at Londolozi in awe.

California native, travel junkie, animal lover...... have traveled to Africa over a dozen times to fulfill my passion for observing animals in their natural environment. Londolozi has become my favorite place to stay, with almost yearly visits since 2019.

Love nature, watching animals and going on safari. Been lots of times on safari to different African countries. Londolozi is one of my favourite places. I am always looking forward to my next trip to Londolozi!

Wildlife Photography Enthusiast

That is me with the amazing John Varty in my profile photo.

Looking forward to visiting Londolozi for the first time in Sept. 2023!  Update: it was spectacular. Kyle was an amazing ranger/guide with Prof as his formidable tracker! So many sightings every day!  We look forward to our next visit.
Retired from consumer product marketing. Hobbies are sculpture, care of community perennial garden in 7 acre private park, member of several community boards.

I am a published author and wildlife and travel writer, specializing is African safaris.  I have always had a deep affinity with all living creatures, even while growing up in urban Amsterdam. Going on safari has enhanced that innate connection into a lifelong passion.
Passionate about wildlife conservation and Big Cats!   Travel, family, reading, hiking, skiing, safaris!
South African living in Canada for the past +25 years, lover of the African bush!

I live in the US but I am from Argentina. Africa has conquered my heart! Kenya, Botswana, Zimbabwe, and now South Africa. Following the concept of wildness from Craig Foster... So much to learn from traditional cultures throughout the world!
I was a physicist in my professional life. I treasure the everlasting connections with many of my former students...
First visited Londolozi in June 2011.  My profile picture up close with the Nkuwa female during our 2023 visit. We returned again in 2025.  Can't wait to come back again!

I am a published writer of three non fiction books, including My Life With Leopards, the Graham Cooke Story, which was set at Londolozi in the early 1990s. acf.lol_basic_profile_excerpt: Daughter of Sunset Bend, her rich golden coat and presence around camp defined an era of Londolozi's leopard dynasty through her offspring.
acf.lol_basic_profile_content:
Heritage & Lineage
Born in December 1997 to the Sunset Bend Female, the Vomba Female was the only surviving cub from her mother’s first litter. She inherited and amplified the distinctive golden coat of the Sunset Bend lineage, eventually becoming a pivotal figure in establishing this bloodline’s prominence at Londolozi through her successful daughters.

Territory
Her territory evolved throughout her life:

Initially established west of Londolozi camps
Expanded to control prime territory along the entire Sand River frontage
Gradually ceded portions to her daughters:

Western section to Tutlwa Female (2006)
Eastern section to Mashaba Female (2008)

The final years centred around Londolozi camps along the southern bank of Sand River
Notable for incorporating camp into her territory, regularly patrolling through.

Physical Characteristics

3:2 spot pattern
Distinctive rich golden coat characteristic of Sunset Bend lineage
Long face and tail
Emerald eyes

Reproductive History
Demonstrated remarkable persistence in reproduction despite numerous setbacks:
Successful Offspring:

2003: Vomba Young Female (one of two, sibling killed by hyena)
2006: Tutlwa Female (one survived from a litter of two)
2008: Mashaba Female (single cub)

Other Attempts:

2002: Two cubs (both lost)
2004: Two cubs (both lost)
2005: Two cubs (litter disappeared)
2008: Two cubs (presumed dead)
2009: Suspected den near Pioneer Camp (cubs never seen)
2011: Suspected den near Tree Camp (cubs never seen)
2012: Final litter – male cub successfully raised to 8 months but disappeared after independence

Behavioural Notes

Masterful hunter, known for ambitious prey selection including pythons
Extremely elusive despite territory around camps
Exceptional use of dense vegetation and drainage lines
Known for remarkable hunting abilities in riverine habitat
Utilizing the camp environment while maintaining wild nature
Notorious for being difficult to track despite proximity to camp
Often detected only through alarm calls of prey species

Historical Significance

A key figure in establishing the prominence of Sunset Bend lineage
Successfully raised multiple female offspring who inherited prime territories
Created dynasty through daughters Tutlwa and Mashaba Females
Demonstrated successful adaptation to human presence while maintaining wild behaviour
Her bloodline continues to influence Londolozi’s leopard population through multiple generations of descendants
Provided unprecedented insights into leopard behaviour around human settlements
Her legacy lives on through at least 5 first or second-generation descendants viewed regularly on Londolozi

Her death in 2013, likely at the hands of the Tsalala Pride, marked the end of an era, but her influence continues through her descendants who maintain the prestigious Sunset Bend lineage’s presence at Londolozi.

acf.lol_territory_desc: The Vomba female, after holding territory from Londolozi's eastern border all the way to the western, towards the end of her life patrolled only a small area from the Sand River southwards to Main Road, at most three kilometres wide. She had ceded off territory to the Tutlwa and Mashaba females, and in her old age consolidated only the central parts of the larger area she once moved through.

Passionate about wildlife.
An Zambian by birth, I am a passionate amateur wildlife photographer, a lover of all things in the African bush and a huge fan of Londolozi and all it offers!

Talley Smith's father. Resident of Bermuda. Huge fan of Londolozi and Africa generally. Keen amateur photographer.

Originally from New York USA currently living in the Sunshine state of Florida in the Tampa Bay area. My first trip to Africa was in 2009 when I visited  Botswana and Zambia. My first trip to Sabi Sands South Africa was in 2011. This is where my true addiction began. I stayed at Londolozi Varty camp and fell in love with the people and the animals.  Since then I have been back six more times and returning Sept. 2023 for my 7th . I have written several blogs and enjoy sharing photos and experiences from my trips. Leopards and male lions are my favorite to photograph. At home I have my own little family including my black lion Myra and two wild dogs Max and Jack.

I came here for the 1st time with my husband in Feb 2010, 2nd stop on a Vic Falls-Londolozi-Cape Town trip. I'd wanted to come here for years, as my ambition was to see a leopard in the wild. We looked at the cost, thought "ouch!" then - well it is just a one-off! On our 1st game drive  we saw Vomba, so mission achieved. Then the next morning we saw Camp Pan mating with Nottens! Within 24 hours of arriving we were completely smitten, and knew we not only had to come back, but come back the next year. So began a highly expensive addiction, and my trip 3 weeks ago was my 9th consecutive year and I celebrated my 100th game drive!
Alan and I have been ambassadors for many years, this is our favorite place on earth ?

Bob and I live in the San Francisco Bay Area where we enjoy boating, hiking, photography and travel. After many trips to Eastern and Southern Africa, we are pleased to call Londolozi our 'African home!'

Megan grew up at Londolozi, where her love for nature blossomed. With a degree in Visual Studies and Social Media Marketing, her journey came full circle when she joined the dynamic Londolozi Creative Hub, where her love for nature and visuals finds its perfect home. 

Guided by an unwavering love for photography, videography, and the captivating realm of visuals, Megan hopes to impart a unique and vibrant essence to each of the creative projects she takes on.

acf.lol_basic_profile_excerpt: Londolozi's oldest territorial female. Distinguished by her nose spot, this Sunsetbend matriarch's legacy lives on through her daughters.
acf.lol_basic_profile_content:
Heritage & Lineage

Born in September 2008 to the Vomba Female and sired by the Camp Pan Male, the Mashaba Female carries the distinctive golden coat characteristic of the Sunsetbend lineage. She represents one of the most successful branches of this prestigious bloodline at Londolozi.

Territory

Originally establishing herself around the Londolozi camps, her territory has shifted significantly over the years. In late 2018, she began moving southward, initially occupying the area left vacant by the deceased Tamboti Female. Currently, she holds territory in the area formerly occupied by the Tatowa Female, demonstrating the dynamic nature of leopard territorial behaviour.

Physical Characteristics

Distinctive spot in the pink of her nose
Notable striations in her irises
Classic 3:3 spot pattern
Golden coat characteristic of the Sunsetbend lineage

Reproductive History

The Mashaba Female has shown remarkable persistence in reproduction, though faced with significant challenges. Her reproductive history includes:

Successful Offspring:

Nkoveni Female (August 2012)
Ximungwe Female (May 2015)

Notable Attempts:

Twelve documented litters between 2012 and 2023, totalling more than 30 cubs
Demonstrated exceptional resilience in continuing to reproduce despite numerous setbacks

Current Status

As of 2024, she holds the distinction of being Londolozi’s oldest territorial female. Despite her age, she continues to demonstrate remarkable resilience and adaptability, maintaining her territory and attempting to reproduce. Her successful offspring, particularly the Nkoveni and Ximungwe females, have themselves established territories and produced cubs, ensuring the continuation of her lineage.

Behavioural Notes

The Mashaba Female exemplifies the adaptability of leopards, having successfully adjusted her territory multiple times throughout her life in response to changing dynamics and pressure from other leopards. Her longevity and successful raising of two female cubs to independence have made her one of the most significant contributors to Londolozi’s current leopard population.

Historical Significance

Her life story spans a significant period in Londolozi’s leopard history. Through her daughters and their offspring, she has played a crucial role in maintaining the prestigious Sunsetbend lineage. Her bloodline continues to influence the leopard dynamics of the reserve, with her descendants now raising cubs of their own.

acf.lol_territory_desc: The Mashaba female's territory is centred in the area around the Londolozi camps; she is an almost constant presence in the riverine bush and bushwillow-covered hillsides where she uses the drainage lines to move between key areas in her territory.  The drainage lines which form a key part of her territory are also ideal hunting grounds for impala, bushbuck and nyala antelope which form a core component of her diet.

Amanda is the Head of Marketing at Londolozi & has been in the marketing & creative industry for 16 years & the health and wellness industry for 10 years. She holds a Bachelor’s degree in Psychology and Journalism from The University of Cape Town & an Honours degree in Brand Management. She's a Life Coach, an Enneagram Practitioner & Londolozi's photographer in residence. Her passion for the creative world, wilderness & wellness has led to a unique role within the Londolozi Family. She spearheaded the creation of the Photographic Studio & brings specialty retreat offerings to life at Londolozi. Amanda ensures that marketing always has deep experience at its roots.
The Londolozi Photo Studio

Mike Nicki Harry and Toby, we try to visit Londo once a year. We think of it as our second home and are privileged to have seen the most amazing sights, encountered wonderful animals and learned so much about the bush from some amazing guides and trackers with such knowledge.

Passionate Londolozi Guests! Avid wildlife photographers. Supporters and advocates for the Good Work Foundation through the All Heart Fund in the USA. Restaurateurs and wine & spirits retailers in Sarasota, Florida at Michael’s On East (www.bestfood.com)

For the past 35 years I've been amazed and inspired by wildlife from all corners of the world. Following a career in the City of London I now dedicate my time to wildlife photographer and commitment to wildlife conservation. When not travelling I volunteer for Conservation Organisations based in London. Social Media - www.janeaddey.co.uk & @addeyphotos.
Passionate about wildlife.

I had dreamed of going to Londolozi for years and finally did it August 2017! This experience was way above and beyond anything that I could have ever imagined and I can't wait to go back. A big case of Bush Bug! A truly life changing experience in so many ways.
I live in NY, work as a nurse, volunteer at an animal sanctuary, am an animal rights activist and a vegetarian.....the idea of living guided is intriguing my soul as my passion for animals is stronger than anything else in my world.....

I arrived at Londolozi on 1 st December 1998. I was a trainee ranger and I was green behind the ears. Londolozi became my family and my home. I left in 2005 and returned later that year to get married down in the Sand River at Londolozi. I have been very fotunate to return with my wife every year since then and I have a son who is mad about tracking and anti-poaching thanks to the many hours he has spent wit me in the bush.
Hopelessly addicted and devoted to leopards.

Born in New York and settled down in Hong Kong for the past 20 years after living in London and Tokyo.  I "found" Londolozi in 2009 and have been a regular visitor since.  Over that time I have gained a passion for the bush and the photographic opportunities it provides.  Thanks to the tutelage of the Londolozi rangers and Creative hub I am getting my photography to an acceptable level.
Following my passion for wildlife and photography

Work with innovative technology. Based in UK. Have lived in Africa and the Middle East. Passionate about travel, wildlife and photography. Keeping a log of all leopard sightings during trips to Londolozi over last few years!
Talley Smith's father. Resident of Bermuda. Huge fan of Londolozi and Africa generally. Keen amateur photographer.

When I was 25, I spent 15 months in South Africa, in a small town called Harrismith well known to those who drive from Johannesburg to Durban as it is a classic pit stop to refuel. It is then that I first heard about Londolozi when I bought the book "the leopards of Londolozi" and promised myself that 1 day I could fulfill my dream of visiting. It took me exactly 20 years after I had moved back to France and in April 2017, at last, I brought my wife and 9-year son Antoine to what I now consider to be the nicest place on earth: Londolozi. As I couldn't help myself, we came back this year for another 4 days of pure happiness

James had hardly touched a camera when he came to Londolozi, but his writing skills that complemented his Honours degree in Zoology meant that he was quickly snapped up by the Londolozi blog team. 

An environment rich in photographers helped him develop the photographic skills he needed to start capturing some great images, and 2015 saw him make the move from stills photography into film as well.

James was a member of the Londolozi family from 2010 - 2021.

We looked at the cost, thought "ouch!" then - well it is just a one-off! On our 1st game drive  we saw Vomba, so mission achieved. Then the next morning we saw Camp Pan mating with Nottens! Within 24 hours of arriving we were completely smitten, and knew we not only had to come back, but come back the next year. So began a highly expensive addiction, and my trip 3 weeks ago was my 9th consecutive year and I celebrated my 100th game drive!

Our first visit was in 2011, we returned in 2014, then again in 2017, and again in 2018.  It is favorite place to be.  We plan on coming 2020 for my 70th birthday (3/2/50) and our 50th wedding anniversary (9/5/70)
We recently visited with our daughter's family, including 8 yr old granddaughter.  She is still talking about all the wonderful things that she saw on Safari.  We were worried that it might be a little gory for her, but she reacted with vigor to the most gruesome of events.  We plan a return visit in 2020 - that will be our 5th trip to visit this incredible place where the guides, trackers, and all the staff make this such a memorable experience for all that visit.

I left a successful corporate career 18 months ago to explore my passion for the bush.  The last year has been incredible having completed my field guide training and travelled extensively to some of Southern Africa's best safari destinations!
I love animals! A big intrest of mine is to play golf. I love to travel.

A Psychiatrist from Salt Lake City, Utah in the United States. Together with his classical pianist wife, Janet Mann, he loves travel to all of the beautiful places on Earth.  He is passionate about animals and plants, seeing them and protecting them.  He is a tireless advocate for a “Green New Deal” to combat climate change in combination with restructuring society and the economy. He loved every aspect of his visit to Londolozi, from the magnificent accommodations and surroundings, the terrific food and atmosphere in the BOMA, the Varty family ideal of providing a great experience to tourists while taking care of the animals, taking care of the land, and taking care of local people.

Lucie and I are retired and have turned our energies to photography and videography, of which wildlife is by far the favorite subject.  We have been to Africa every 2-3 years over the last 35 years.  We have been to several camps in each of South Africa, Botswana, Kenya, Tanzania, Namibia, Uganda and Rwanda but Londolozi and Tiger Canyon are our go-to favorite places.  We are unabashedly predator-centric and aviary-sated.  And we are so thankful that the Varty family built this community-driven concept and has taught us all the meaning of "ubuntu".

Being surrounded by wilderness from a young age, you experience it in all of its essence. Matt was privileged enough to grow up in the Lowveld and its surroundings, sparking a great love for nature and all it has to offer, be it the sunsets, vast landscapes or amazing wildlife. As a young boy, his favourite trips were always going to the bush with family, spending time with only the best that Africa has to offer.

Matt discovered a passion that went hand-in-hand with his love for wildlife, Photography, and this is how he found his path leading to Londolozi from 2016 to 2020.

Richie is Londolozi's Director of Technology and Sustainability and the founder of the Londolozi blog. Over the past decade he has built Londolozi's online ecosystem into a platform for advocacy of the restoration and rewilding of the natural world. Today he applies that same thinking to the land itself, helping lead the Save the Sand initiative to restore the Sand River catchment that gives Londolozi its lifeblood. His work lives at the meeting point of ancient wisdom, modern technology and nature. You'll find him in the LCH at Londolozi. Come say hi on your next visit.

Jemma grew up on a farm in the Midlands Meander in Kwa-Zulu Natal and studied at the University of Cape Town. With little bush experience but with many hours of au pairing, teaching English and forming a love for travel, Jemma found herself working at Londolozi as the Cubs Den Manager in January 2018. A few months later she started working for the Londolozi Creative Hub in Digital Marketing, the person behind the scenes of Londolozi's Blog and social media - and she hasn't looked back since...
Passionate about wildlife conservation and Big Cats!   Travel, family, reading, hiking, skiing, safaris!

Bronwyn is 4th generation custodian of Londolozi Game Reserve, a mother, Master life coach and also one of its most longstanding employees, having grown up on the floors of the kitchen and in the gardens of the lodge.  Bronwyn’s official title is that of Londolozi’s Creative Director and as such she has spearheaded the reinvention of the Londolozi brand from 2007 until present day. In 2018, Bronwyn led the creation of the Londolozi Healing House, establishing one of the safari industry’s most innovative wellness offerings.  By weaving healing, mindfulness, and nature-based transformation into the guest experience, she helped reinvent the concept of wilderness wellness in the safari space.

Love nature, watching animals and going on safari. Been lots of times on safari to different African countries. Londolozi is one of my favourite places. I am always looking forward to my next trip to Londolozi!
I love big cats (animals as well), cricket, and food.

As a former travel agency owner specializing is conservation tourism, I have the opportunity to travel to unique places globally. With so many places to experience, I never go to the same place twice - Until Londolozi. The people, the land and the experiences stole a piece of my heart. Whenever I find myself in Southern Africa, I make a point to find my way back.

I'm a free lance Home Economist working mostly on Masterchef a BBC cookery show. I live in England with my husband and two black Labradors. We have three grown up sons, one grandson and  granddaughter . We have visited Londolozi four times and are making a fifth visit in early June and we cant wait!!

As a young boy growing up on an agricultural farm in Zimbabwe, Sean spent every opportunity entertaining himself outdoors, camping in the local nature reserve and learning about all facets of the natural world.  

After completing a Bachelor of Science degree in Environmental Science in Cape Town, Sean was free to follow his nature ambitions and return to his bush-loving childhood dreams, which led him to Londolozi.

Going into semi-retirement on the guiding front in 2020 saw Sean settle into a far more permanent role in the LCH, focusing his efforts on producing media content for the Londolozi online space.

Garrett has always had an incredible love for the wilderness and found his way to Londolozi straight after University. After spending time as a Londolozi Camp Manager, the incredible stories of daily sightings from his ranger counterparts and guests alike pushed him to become a Londolozi Guide, where he enjoyed 3 years in the field sharing Londolozi with thousands of guests. After a brief sabbatical travelling through Southern Africa and working in Tanzania, Garrett returned to the Londolozi Family as Sales Manager sharing Londolozi with as many people as possible.

Nick was a ranger at Londolozi from 2018 - 2022. He always had a love for nature. Growing up in Johannesburg, the annual family trip to the bush (particularly the Kruger Lowveld region of South Africa) became an escape from city life. When he and his brother weren't physically in the bush, they would pretend they were by watching wildlife documentaries and making animal tracks in the garden at home. After high school, Nick spent a year teaching sport in England and then returned to South Africa to study Engineering at Stellenbosch University. It was in the mountains of Stellenbosch where Nick further cultivated his passion for nature.

Robbie developed a passion for the African bush from many visits to his family’s small holding in a greater conservancy just outside Johannesburg. Living in the big city his whole life, he always found refuge in the outdoors and has grown to appreciate the slower pace of life and connectivity with nature that comes with spending time in the bush. After completing his studies in Finance and Accounting at university in Cape Town he leapt at the opportunity to follow his dream by partaking in Londolozi’s 2020 ranger training programme. His dream of sharing his passion for the African bush with others is being lived and will continue to evolve as he furthers his career as a guide at Londolozi.

Robyn grew up in Johannesburg and every family holiday was spent exploring the Lowveld or camping around Southern Africa. Her love of nature and conservation propelled her to complete her Masters degree at the University of Edinburgh’s school of Geoscience. Although this gave her a great understanding of world-wide ecological processes, she wanted to develop a better knowledge of smaller elements in the environment closer to home - birds, trees, animals and the landscape in South Africa. This lead her back to the Lowveld and to the place where her love of nature was originally ignited when she was younger.

Growing up in the small coastal town of Mtunzini, Matt's childhood was shaped by endless hours spent exploring the forests, beaches and wetlands that sparked a lifelong passion for wildlife. After completing a BSc degree, he worked in construction and landscaping before the opportunity to join Londolozi changed the course of his career. Today, as a ranger and wildlife photographer, he has the privilege of spending every day immersed in the wilderness that first inspired him as a child.

Megan grew up at Londolozi, where her love for nature blossomed. With a degree in Visual Studies and Social Media Marketing, her journey came full circle when she joined the dynamic Londolozi Creative Hub, where her love for nature and visuals finds its perfect home. 

Guided by an unwavering love for photography, videography, and the captivating realm of visuals, Megan hopes to impart a unique and vibrant essence to each of the creative projects she takes on.

After a few years of working in the world of economic consulting, Kate’s love of adventure, wilderness and sense of curiosity led her to move away from the city and join the Londolozi guiding team.  It was amidst her years of studying politics, philosophy and economics that her love of exploring and understanding different wilderness areas in South Africa compounded through trips with friends and family. Kate has been fortunate to travel to many different corners of the world but she’ll argue that nothing quite beats being surrounded by nature watching an African sunrise or sunset, especially at Londolozi!

Nick grew up in Johannesburg with a deep love for the outdoors. After finishing high school, he spent a formative gap year in the Zimbabwean bushveld — an experience that cemented his passion for wildlife and conservation. Although he went on to study and build a career in corporate real estate, the pull of the wilderness never faded. Now an experienced member of the Londolozi guiding team, Nick finds the greatest joy in tracking leopards and immersing himself in the intricate world of birding. He has developed a strong passion for wildlife photography, always looking to capture authentic moments in the wild.

Keagan has always had a connection with wildlife, having been lucky enough to visit Londolozi as a child. After growing up in Johannesburg, he attended boarding school in the KwaZulu Natal Midlands where weekends were spent exploring the reserve and appreciating his surroundings. Keagan further went on to study Engineering at the University of Cape Town, during which each holiday was spent with either family or friends in the Lowveld, solidifying his dream of becoming a ranger. Having joined the Londolozi team, he is now fulfilling his childhood dream of living and working in the African bush.

California native, travel junkie, animal lover...... have traveled to Africa over a dozen times to fulfill my passion for observing animals in their natural environment. Londolozi has become my favorite place to stay, with almost yearly visits since 2019.

I am a published author and wildlife and travel writer, specializing is African safaris.  I have always had a deep affinity with all living creatures, even while growing up in urban Amsterdam. Going on safari has enhanced that innate connection into a lifelong passion.

I am a published writer of three non fiction books, including My Life With Leopards, the Graham Cooke Story, which was set at Londolozi in the early 1990s. I am a seasoned safari traveller, contributing publications of safari lodges and destinations to various magazines and a keen safari photographer.

Born in New York and settled down in Hong Kong for the past 20 years after living in London and Tokyo.  I "found" Londolozi in 2009 and have been a regular visitor since.  Over that time I have gained a passion for the bush and the photographic opportunities it provides.  Thanks to the tutelage of the Londolozi rangers and Creative hub I am getting my photography to an acceptable level.
Following my passion for wildlife and photography

Work with innovative technology. Based in UK. Have lived in Africa and the Middle East. Passionate about travel, wildlife and photography. Keeping a log of all leopard sightings during trips to Londolozi over last few years!
Talley Smith's father. Resident of Bermuda. Huge fan of Londolozi and Africa generally. Keen amateur photographer.

When I was 25, I spent 15 months in South Africa, in a small town called Harrismith well known to those who drive from Johannesburg to Durban as it is a classic pit stop to refuel. It is then that I first heard about Londolozi when I bought the book "the leopards of Londolozi" and promised myself that 1 day I could fulfill my dream of visiting. It took me exactly 20 years after I had moved back to France and in April 2017, at last, I brought my wife and 9-year son Antoine to what I now consider to be the nicest place on earth: Londolozi. As I couldn't help myself, we came back this year for another 4 days of pure happiness

James had hardly touched a camera when he came to Londolozi, but his writing skills that complemented his Honours degree in Zoology meant that he was quickly snapped up by the Londolozi blog team. 

An environment rich in photographers helped him develop the photographic skills he needed to start capturing some great images, and 2015 saw him make the move from stills photography into film as well.

James was a member of the Londolozi family from 2010 - 2021.

Originally from New York USA currently living in the Sunshine state of Florida in the Tampa Bay area. My first trip to Africa was in 2009 when I visited  Botswana and Zambia. My first trip to Sabi Sands South Africa was in 2011. This is where my true addiction began. I stayed at Londolozi Varty camp and fell in love with the people and the animals.  Since then I have been back six more times and returning Sept. 2023 for my 7th . I have written several blogs and enjoy sharing photos and experiences from my trips. Leopards and male lions are my favorite to photograph. At home I have my own little family including my black lion Myra and two wild dogs Max and Jack.
Alan and I have been ambassadors for many years, this is our favorite place on earth ?

I came here for the 1st time with my husband in Feb 2010, 2nd stop on a Vic Falls-Londolozi-Cape Town trip. I'd wanted to come here for years, as my ambition was to see a leopard in the wild. We looked at the cost, thought "ouch!" then - well it is just a one-off! On our 1st game drive  we saw Vomba, so mission achieved. Then the next morning we saw Camp Pan mating with Nottens! Within 24 hours of arriving we were completely smitten, and knew we not only had to come back, but come back the next year. So began a highly expensive addiction, and my trip 3 weeks ago was my 9th consecutive year and I celebrated my 100th game drive!

Our first visit was in 2011, we returned in 2014, then again in 2017, and again in 2018.  It is favorite place to be.  We plan on coming 2020 for my 70th birthday (3/2/50) and our 50th wedding anniversary (9/5/70)
We recently visited with our daughter's family, including 8 yr old granddaughter.  She is still talking about all the wonderful things that she saw on Safari.  We were worried that it might be a little gory for her, but she reacted with vigor to the most gruesome of events.  We plan a return visit in 2020 - that will be our 5th trip to visit this incredible place where the guides, trackers, and all the staff make this such a memorable experience for all that visit.

I left a successful corporate career 18 months ago to explore my passion for the bush.  The last year has been incredible having completed my field guide training and travelled extensively to some of Southern Africa's best safari destinations!
I love animals! A big intrest of mine is to play golf. I love to travel.

A Psychiatrist from Salt Lake City, Utah in the United States. Together with his classical pianist wife, Janet Mann, he loves travel to all of the beautiful places on Earth.  He is passionate about animals and plants, seeing them and protecting them.  He is a tireless advocate for a “Green New Deal” to combat climate change in combination with restructuring society and the economy. He loved every aspect of his visit to Londolozi, from the magnificent accommodations and surroundings, the terrific food and atmosphere in the BOMA, the Varty family ideal of providing a great experience to tourists while taking care of the animals, taking care of the land, and taking care of local people.

Lucie and I are retired and have turned our energies to photography and videography, of which wildlife is by far the favorite subject.  We have been to Africa every 2-3 years over the last 35 years.  We have been to several camps in each of South Africa, Botswana, Kenya, Tanzania, Namibia, Uganda and Rwanda but Londolozi and Tiger Canyon are our go-to favorite places.  We are unabashedly predator-centric and aviary-sated.  And we are so thankful that the Varty family built this community-driven concept and has taught us all the meaning of "ubuntu".

Being surrounded by wilderness from a young age, you experience it in all of its essence. Matt was privileged enough to grow up in the Lowveld and its surroundings, sparking a great love for nature and all it has to offer, be it the sunsets, vast landscapes or amazing wildlife. As a young boy, his favourite trips were always going to the bush with family, spending time with only the best that Africa has to offer.

Matt discovered a passion that went hand-in-hand with his love for wildlife, Photography, and this is how he found his path leading to Londolozi from 2016 to 2020.

Richie is Londolozi's Director of Technology and Sustainability and the founder of the Londolozi blog. Over the past decade he has built Londolozi's online ecosystem into a platform for advocacy of the restoration and rewilding of the natural world. Today he applies that same thinking to the land itself, helping lead the Save the Sand initiative to restore the Sand River catchment that gives Londolozi its lifeblood. His work lives at the meeting point of ancient wisdom, modern technology and nature. You'll find him in the LCH at Londolozi. Come say hi on your next visit.

Jemma grew up on a farm in the Midlands Meander in Kwa-Zulu Natal and studied at the University of Cape Town. With little bush experience but with many hours of au pairing, teaching English and forming a love for travel, Jemma found herself working at Londolozi as the Cubs Den Manager in January 2018. A few months later she started working for the Londolozi Creative Hub in Digital Marketing, the person behind the scenes of Londolozi's Blog and social media - and she hasn't looked back since...
Passionate about wildlife conservation and Big Cats!   Travel, family, reading, hiking, skiing, safaris!

Bronwyn is 4th generation custodian of Londolozi Game Reserve, a mother, Master life coach and also one of its most longstanding employees, having grown up on the floors of the kitchen and in the gardens of the lodge.  Bronwyn’s official title is that of Londolozi’s Creative Director and as such she has spearheaded the reinvention of the Londolozi brand from 2007 until present day. In 2018, Bronwyn led the creation of the Londolozi Healing House, establishing one of the safari industry’s most innovative wellness offerings.  By weaving healing, mindfulness, and nature-based transformation into the guest experience, she helped reinvent the concept of wilderness wellness in the safari space.

Love nature, watching animals and going on safari. Been lots of times on safari to different African countries. Londolozi is one of my favourite places. I am always looking forward to my next trip to Londolozi!
I love big cats (animals as well), cricket, and food.

As a former travel agency owner specializing is conservation tourism, I have the opportunity to travel to unique places globally. With so many places to experience, I never go to the same place twice - Until Londolozi. The people, the land and the experiences stole a piece of my heart. Whenever I find myself in Southern Africa, I make a point to find my way back.

I'm a free lance Home Economist working mostly on Masterchef a BBC cookery show. I live in England with my husband and two black Labradors. We have three grown up sons, one grandson and  granddaughter . We have visited Londolozi four times and are making a fifth visit in early June and we cant wait!!

As a young boy growing up on an agricultural farm in Zimbabwe, Sean spent every opportunity entertaining himself outdoors, camping in the local nature reserve and learning about all facets of the natural world.  

After completing a Bachelor of Science degree in Environmental Science in Cape Town, Sean was free to follow his nature ambitions and return to his bush-loving childhood dreams, which led him to Londolozi.

Going into semi-retirement on the guiding front in 2020 saw Sean settle into a far more permanent role in the LCH, focusing his efforts on producing media content for the Londolozi online space.

Garrett has always had an incredible love for the wilderness and found his way to Londolozi straight after University. After spending time as a Londolozi Camp Manager, the incredible stories of daily sightings from his ranger counterparts and guests alike pushed him to become a Londolozi Guide, where he enjoyed 3 years in the field sharing Londolozi with thousands of guests. After a brief sabbatical travelling through Southern Africa and working in Tanzania, Garrett returned to the Londolozi Family as Sales Manager sharing Londolozi with as many people as possible.

Nick was a ranger at Londolozi from 2018 - 2022. He always had a love for nature. Growing up in Johannesburg, the annual family trip to the bush (particularly the Kruger Lowveld region of South Africa) became an escape from city life. When he and his brother weren't physically in the bush, they would pretend they were by watching wildlife documentaries and making animal tracks in the garden at home. After high school, Nick spent a year teaching sport in England and then returned to South Africa to study Engineering at Stellenbosch University. It was in the mountains of Stellenbosch where Nick further cultivated his passion for nature.

Robbie developed a passion for the African bush from many visits to his family’s small holding in a greater conservancy just outside Johannesburg. Living in the big city his whole life, he always found refuge in the outdoors and has grown to appreciate the slower pace of life and connectivity with nature that comes with spending time in the bush. After completing his studies in Finance and Accounting at university in Cape Town he leapt at the opportunity to follow his dream by partaking in Londolozi’s 2020 ranger training programme. His dream of sharing his passion for the African bush with others is being lived and will continue to evolve as he furthers his career as a guide at Londolozi.

Robyn grew up in Johannesburg and every family holiday was spent exploring the Lowveld or camping around Southern Africa. Her love of nature and conservation propelled her to complete her Masters degree at the University of Edinburgh’s school of Geoscience. Although this gave her a great understanding of world-wide ecological processes, she wanted to develop a better knowledge of smaller elements in the environment closer to home - birds, trees, animals and the landscape in South Africa. This lead her back to the Lowveld and to the place where her love of nature was originally ignited when she was younger.

Growing up in the small coastal town of Mtunzini, Matt's childhood was shaped by endless hours spent exploring the forests, beaches and wetlands that sparked a lifelong passion for wildlife. After completing a BSc degree, he worked in construction and landscaping before the opportunity to join Londolozi changed the course of his career. Today, as a ranger and wildlife photographer, he has the privilege of spending every day immersed in the wilderness that first inspired him as a child.

Megan grew up at Londolozi, where her love for nature blossomed. With a degree in Visual Studies and Social Media Marketing, her journey came full circle when she joined the dynamic Londolozi Creative Hub, where her love for nature and visuals finds its perfect home. 

Guided by an unwavering love for photography, videography, and the captivating realm of visuals, Megan hopes to impart a unique and vibrant essence to each of the creative projects she takes on.

After a few years of working in the world of economic consulting, Kate’s love of adventure, wilderness and sense of curiosity led her to move away from the city and join the Londolozi guiding team.  It was amidst her years of studying politics, philosophy and economics that her love of exploring and understanding different wilderness areas in South Africa compounded through trips with friends and family. Kate has been fortunate to travel to many different corners of the world but she’ll argue that nothing quite beats being surrounded by nature watching an African sunrise or sunset, especially at Londolozi!

Nick grew up in Johannesburg with a deep love for the outdoors. After finishing high school, he spent a formative gap year in the Zimbabwean bushveld — an experience that cemented his passion for wildlife and conservation. Although he went on to study and build a career in corporate real estate, the pull of the wilderness never faded. Now an experienced member of the Londolozi guiding team, Nick finds the greatest joy in tracking leopards and immersing himself in the intricate world of birding. He has developed a strong passion for wildlife photography, always looking to capture authentic moments in the wild.

Keagan has always had a connection with wildlife, having been lucky enough to visit Londolozi as a child. After growing up in Johannesburg, he attended boarding school in the KwaZulu Natal Midlands where weekends were spent exploring the reserve and appreciating his surroundings. Keagan further went on to study Engineering at the University of Cape Town, during which each holiday was spent with either family or friends in the Lowveld, solidifying his dream of becoming a ranger. Having joined the Londolozi team, he is now fulfilling his childhood dream of living and working in the African bush.

California native, travel junkie, animal lover...... have traveled to Africa over a dozen times to fulfill my passion for observing animals in their natural environment. Londolozi has become my favorite place to stay, with almost yearly visits since 2019.

I am a published author and wildlife and travel writer, specializing is African safaris.  I have always had a deep affinity with all living creatures, even while growing up in urban Amsterdam. Going on safari has enhanced that innate connection into a lifelong passion.

I am a published writer of three non fiction books, including My Life With Leopards, the Graham Cooke Story, which was set at Londolozi in the early 1990s. I am a seasoned safari traveller, contributing publications of safari lodges and destinations to various magazines and a keen safari photographer.

acf.lol_basic_profile_excerpt: The Tu Tones male astounded everyone by establishing his territory within his father Camp Pan's territory.
acf.lol_basic_profile_content:
Originally the Maxabene 3:2 young male, and born in the same litter as the Makhotini male, the Tu-Tones male was an individual that single-handedly rewrote the textbooks on leopard behaviour.

His movements upon independence were probably a result of a combination of factors, but essentially what happened was that he didn’t disperse as young males generally do, but instead stayed pretty much within the confines of his father’s territory. Another behavioural anomaly was that his father (the Camp Pan male) seemed to accept his presence; although there was some snarling and aggression towards each other when they met, there was no physical confrontation witnessed. The death of his mother and the fact that the one female cub she raised to independence had dispersed a long way away meant that there was no real genetic pressure for him to disperse either.

Whatever the case, the Tu-Tones male was an almost constant presence in the territory controlled by the Camp Pan male, and the two were even seen sharing mating rights with the Tamboti female on at least two separate occasions.

Unfortunately for this young male, his unusual co-territorial occupation with his father was to be his downfall, as once the Camp Pan male became unseated in 2014 by the Piva male, the Tu-Tones male, having not been properly territorial himself, seems to have been unable to maintain any kind of hold on the territory his father had been defending, and was forced into a nomadic lifestyle almost overnight. His condition deteriorated very quickly from there, and he was last seen on Londolozi in the late Summer of 2015.

He was found dead to the east of our boundary in late March of that year, and tracks in the area suggested that a troop of baboons had killed him. His emaciated condition would have made him incredibly vulnerable.

acf.lol_territory_desc: A remarkable story in which this leopard established his territory in eastern Sparta within the territory of his father (something that is typical of female but not male leopards). He died prematurely at the age of 7, close to the time of death of his father and thus we were not able to see how the extension of his territory would have played out.

acf.lol_basic_profile_excerpt: Born 1995 to legendary 3:4 Female. Record holder as Londolozi's oldest leopard at 18 years, embodying the resilience of her royal lineage.
acf.lol_basic_profile_content:
First cub of the famous 3:4 Female

Heritage & Lineage
Born in October 1995 to the legendary 3:4 Female, representing the third generation of the Mother Leopard’s lineage. Her birth in Schweinn Donga marked the continuation of one of Londolozi’s most prestigious leopard bloodlines.

Territory
Initially established territory south of her mother’s range, but later expanded after 3:4’s death in 2009 to incorporate her mother’s former territory. Known for ranging widely, from eastern borders to deep southern reaches, making her sometimes difficult to locate.

Physical Characteristics

5:5 spot pattern
Large pale body typical of Mother Leopard descendants
Dark alluring eyes
Distinctive ageing features in later years

Reproductive History
Despite multiple attempts throughout her life:

1998: First and most successful litter – two females reached independence (including Piva Female)
2001: Two cubs (both lost)
2002: Two cubs (both lost)
2003: Two cubs (fate uncertain)
2005: Two cubs (one taken by Martial Eagle)
2008: Two cubs (both lost)
Multiple mating attempts in later years (2009-2012) proved unsuccessful

Behavioural Notes
Demonstrated remarkable adaptability in her later years, shifting territories as she aged and felt pressure from younger females. Known for being difficult to track and follow, requiring dedicated effort from rangers to locate her. Continued to attempt reproduction well into her senior years, showing strong maternal drive even when physically past prime breeding age.

Historical Significance

Set longevity record at Londolozi, living for 18 years
Represented a crucial link in Mother Leopard’s lineage
Successfully continued bloodline through Piva Female
Demonstrated exceptional survival skills in a predator-rich environment
Final days provided insights into natural end-of-life behaviour in wild leopards
Last seen in poor condition attempting to raid Camp Pan Male’s kill

Her legacy lived on through the Piva Female, maintaining the prestigious bloodline of the original Mother Leopard. Her long life and persistence in attempting reproduction into old age provided valuable insights into leopard behaviour and ageing in the wild.

acf.lol_territory_desc: Upon reaching independence this female established a territory south of Dudley on the Nottens property after which she was named. Upon the demise of her mother, she shifted her territory back northwards into central Dudley, incorporating her late mother's territory. There are many reasons this area is so ideal for leopards; one being that the band of rocky outcrops and boulders found in it form perfect den sites.

section_territory.lol_territory_desc: Upon reaching independence this female established a territory south of Dudley on the Nottens property after which she was named. Upon the demise of her mother, she shifted her territory back northwards into central Dudley, incorporating her late mother's territory. There are many reasons this area is so ideal for leopards; one being that the band of rocky outcrops and boulders found in it form perfect den sites.

users_spotted.user_description: Richie is Londolozi's Director of Technology and Sustainability and the founder of the Londolozi blog. Over the past decade he has built Londolozi's online ecosystem into a platform for advocacy of the restoration and rewilding of the natural world. Today he applies that same thinking to the land itself, helping lead the Save the Sand initiative to restore the Sand River catchment that gives Londolozi its lifeblood. His work lives at the meeting point of ancient wisdom, modern technology and nature. You'll find him in the LCH at Londolozi. Come say hi on your next visit.
An Zambian by birth, I am a passionate amateur wildlife photographer, a lover of all things in the African bush and a huge fan of Londolozi and all it offers!

I came here for the 1st time with my husband in Feb 2010, 2nd stop on a Vic Falls-Londolozi-Cape Town trip. I'd wanted to come here for years, as my ambition was to see a leopard in the wild. We looked at the cost, thought "ouch!" then - well it is just a one-off! On our 1st game drive  we saw Vomba, so mission achieved. Then the next morning we saw Camp Pan mating with Nottens! Within 24 hours of arriving we were completely smitten, and knew we not only had to come back, but come back the next year. So began a highly expensive addiction, and my trip 3 weeks ago was my 9th consecutive year and I celebrated my 100th game drive!
Alan and I have been ambassadors for many years, this is our favorite place on earth ?

Love nature, watching animals and going on safari. Been lots of times on safari to different African countries. Londolozi is one of my favourite places. I am always looking forward to my next trip to Londolozi!

California native, travel junkie, animal lover...... have traveled to Africa over a dozen times to fulfill my passion for observing animals in their natural environment. Londolozi has become my favorite place to stay, with almost yearly visits since 2019.

Nick grew up in Johannesburg with a deep love for the outdoors. After finishing high school, he spent a formative gap year in the Zimbabwean bushveld — an experience that cemented his passion for wildlife and conservation. Although he went on to study and build a career in corporate real estate, the pull of the wilderness never faded. Now an experienced member of the Londolozi guiding team, Nick finds the greatest joy in tracking leopards and immersing himself in the intricate world of birding. He has developed a strong passion for wildlife photography, always looking to capture authentic moments in the wild.

acf.lol_basic_profile_excerpt_alt: The first cub of the legendary 3:4 female, the 5:5 female grew to be the oldest recorded leopard on Londolozi (18yrs)
